questions.question: Assume you're a database administrator of X organization, and you're working on a website that connects to a sales database. The SQL queries are included in some of the pages. Which security danger, if any, do you think you'll be most vulnerable to?
options: No problem, as long as the SQL is password-protected, it is safe.
Hackers do not have a means of accessing the underlying SQL.
There is a risk a hacker would use SQL injection.
questions.explanation: SQL injection is a common attack vector where malicious SQL statements are inserted into input fields. Password protection alone doesn't prevent this attack; proper input sanitization and parameterized queries are needed.

questions.question: Which of the following statement is used to remove the privilege from the user Abebe?
options: Remove update on department from Abebe
Revoke update on employee from Abebe
Delete select on department from Abebe
Grant update on employee from Abebe
questions.explanation: The REVOKE statement is used in SQL to remove privileges from users. The syntax is REVOKE privilege ON object FROM user.

questions.question: ____ is eliminating duplication of tuples.
questions.explanation: The Rename operation in relational algebra eliminates duplicate tuples by giving relations a new name.

questions.question: The basic goal of query optimization is to find the most efficient way of implementing relational algebra operations at the lowest possible cost, so what factors are evaluated to compute the cost of evaluation plan by the optimizer in query processing?
options: CPU cost, I/O cost, and memory cost
questions.explanation: Query optimizers evaluate multiple cost factors including CPU processing time, disk I/O operations, and memory usage to determine the most efficient query execution plan.

questions.question: Assume that if a transaction Tj wants to read a value that has been changed or written by another transaction Ti, Tj's commit must do so after Ti's commit. So, what kinds of recoverable schedules are associated with this scenario?
questions.explanation: Strict schedules ensure that a transaction can only read or write a data item after the transaction that last wrote it has committed, preventing cascading aborts.

questions.question: Consider the following action Transaction SQL>commit; SQL>Rollback; What does rollback can do in the above statement?
options: Turn back or goes back the transaction.
questions.explanation: Rollback undoes all changes made in the current transaction, clears the transaction state, and reverts the database to the state before the transaction began.

questions.question: Which one of the following is distributed database design strategies?
questions.explanation: Distributed database design strategies include fragmentation (splitting data into pieces), replication (copying data to multiple sites), and allocation (distributing data across sites).

questions.question: How can be managed concurrency control in distributed system?
options: By applying locking method and lock managers deal with.
questions.explanation: Concurrency control in distributed systems can be managed through locking mechanisms and timestamp-based methods, both of which help maintain data consistency.

questions.question: Which privileges should a user be given to log on to the Oracle server?
questions.explanation: None of the listed options are directly required for logging on to an Oracle server. Users typically need CREATE SESSION privilege to log in.

questions.question: Which one of the following is cause of transaction Failures?
questions.explanation: Transaction failures can be caused by disk malfunctions (hardware failures), concurrency control enforcement (deadlocks), and transaction errors (logic errors).

questions.question: Which one of the following is the disadvantage of distributed database?
questions.explanation: Distributed databases have disadvantages including security issues (more vulnerable points) and complexity (difficult to manage and maintain).

questions.question: Which of the following depicts the transaction's boundary?
questions.explanation: Transaction boundaries are marked by BEGIN and END statements, which define where a transaction starts and where it ends.

questions.question: After a transaction begins to execute, it enters one of several states, the first of which is the ____ state, in which read or write activities occur.
questions.explanation: The Active state is the first state a transaction enters, where it executes read and write operations.

questions.question: T1 and T2 cannot access the same database at the same time in a ____ level lock transaction, even if they utilize distinct tables.
questions.explanation: At the database level lock, the entire database is locked, preventing other transactions from accessing any part of it even if they use different tables.

questions.question: ____ is a transaction property that determines how transaction integrity is apparent to other users and systems.
questions.explanation: Isolation ensures that the intermediate states of a transaction are not visible to other transactions, making the transaction's integrity apparent to other users and systems.

questions.question: Two-phase locking defines how transactions acquire and relinquish locks.
questions.explanation: Two-phase locking (2PL) is a concurrency control protocol that defines rules for how transactions acquire and release locks in two phases: growing phase and shrinking phase.

questions.question: Concurrency Control Techniques are which of the following?
questions.explanation: Concurrency control techniques include timestamp ordering and locking mechanisms, while recovery is a separate database management function.

questions.question: Which of the following determines Serializability conflicting action?
options: If the action belongs to different transaction
If the action accesses the X item with different read and write operation.
If the action access X item with the action of write operations.
questions.explanation: All conditions can determine conflicting actions in serializability: actions from different transactions, accessing same data item with different operations, and write operations.

questions.question: In ____ scheme, the older transaction rolls back the younger transaction and reschedules it.
questions.explanation: In the wound-wait scheme, if an older transaction requests a lock held by a younger transaction, the younger transaction is 'wounded' (rolled back) and rescheduled.

questions.question: Consider this schedule: S: R1(A), W2(A), Commit2, W1(A), W3(A), Commit3, Commit1. Which of the following statements about the scheduling strategy is correct?
options: The schedule is view serializable schedule and strict recoverable schedule
The schedule is non-serializable schedule and strict recoverable schedule
The schedule is non-serializable schedule and is not strict recoverable schedule.
The Schedule is serializable schedule and is not strict recoverable schedule
questions.explanation: The schedule is non-serializable because the operations cannot be reordered to achieve serial equivalence. It's not strict recoverable because transactions read uncommitted data.

questions.question: The term ____ refers to the process of handling several operations in a database without them interfering with one another.
questions.explanation: Concurrency control manages simultaneous database operations to prevent interference and ensure data consistency.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the basis of ARIES recovery algorithm?
questions.explanation: The ARIES recovery algorithm consists of three phases: Analysis, Redo, and Undo, which work together to recover the database to a consistent state.

questions.question: Concurrency can lead to a slew of issues. If one transaction calculates an aggregate summary function on a number of records while another transaction updates some of those data, the aggregate function may calculate certain values before and after the records are modified. This is referred to as ____ Problems Caused by Concurrency.
questions.explanation: The inconsistent analysis problem occurs when a transaction performing aggregate calculations reads data that is being modified by another transaction, resulting in inconsistent results.

questions.question: Which of the following is likely to result in a deadlock.
questions.explanation: Circular wait is one of the necessary conditions for deadlock, where a set of processes are waiting for resources held by each other in a circular chain.

questions.question: ____ is the process of restoring the database to a correct (consistent) state in the event of a failure.
questions.explanation: Database recovery is the process of restoring the database to a consistent state after a failure using recovery techniques like logging and checkpointing.

questions.question: Which one of the following is distributed database design strategies?
questions.explanation: Distributed database design strategies include fragmentation (splitting data), replication (copying data), and allocation (distributing data).

questions.question: How can be managed concurrency control in distributed system?
options: By applying locking method and lock managers deal with.
questions.explanation: Concurrency control in distributed systems is managed through locking mechanisms and timestamp-based methods. Deadlock is a problem to be avoided, not a control method.

questions.question: Which one of the following is failed under multimedia data?
questions.explanation: Multimedia data includes various types such as images, videos, and audio files, which are all considered multimedia content.

questions.question: Which privileges should a user be given to log on to the Oracle server?
questions.explanation: None of the listed options are directly required for logging on to an Oracle server. Users typically need CREATE SESSION privilege.

questions.question: Which one of the following is cause of transaction Failures?
questions.explanation: Transaction failures can be caused by disk malfunctions, concurrency control enforcement issues (such as deadlocks), and transaction errors.

questions.question: The DB operation in a transaction to update the DB. i.e., insert, update, delete and so on SQL statements is a good example of ____.
questions.explanation: A Write Transaction involves data modification operations such as INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE statements that change the database state.

questions.question: If a schedule is not conflict serializable, it is not possible for there to be an equivalent serial schedule.
questions.explanation: If a schedule is not conflict serializable, there is no way to transform it into a serial schedule by swapping non-conflicting operations, making it impossible to have an equivalent serial schedule.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the disadvantage of distributed database?
questions.explanation: Distributed databases have multiple disadvantages including modularity issues, security concerns, and complexity in management and maintenance.

questions.question: The process of determining the best approach for processing a query is known as ____.
questions.explanation: Query optimization is the process of selecting the most efficient execution plan for a given query from multiple possible alternatives.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a relational algebraic operation that does not form the set theory?
questions.explanation: SELECT is a relational algebra operation but not a set theory operation. UNION, INTERSECTION, and CARTESIAN PRODUCT are set theory operations.

questions.question: Which is the symbol used to denote the SELECT operation?
questions.explanation: The SELECT operation in relational algebra is denoted by the Greek letter Sigma (σ).

questions.question: What will be the number of columns of CARTESIAN PRODUCT if the participating relations have 5 and 7 columns respectively?
questions.explanation: The Cartesian product of two relations results in a relation with the sum of columns from both relations (5 + 7 = 12 columns).

questions.question: The ____ operations are used to add new documents into the collection.
questions.explanation: The Create operation is used to add new documents to a collection in document-based databases like MongoDB.

questions.question: A ____ on a data item can either have locked or unlocked states.
questions.explanation: A Binary lock has only two states: locked (1) and unlocked (0). It's the simplest form of locking mechanism.

questions.question: If all transactions are read-only transactions, then every schedule will be serializable schedules.
questions.explanation: When all transactions are read-only, there are no conflicting operations, so any schedule can be serialized without conflicts.

questions.question: The process of converting data into an unreadable format for those who do not have access to the key is known as ____.
questions.explanation: Encryption transforms readable data into an unreadable format (ciphertext) that can only be accessed with the correct decryption key.

questions.question: A distributed database has which of the following advantages over a centralized database?
questions.explanation: Modular growth is an advantage of distributed databases, allowing organizations to add new sites and expand incrementally without disrupting existing operations.

questions.question: A distributed database is which of the following?
options: A single logical database that is spread to multiple locations and is interconnected by a network
A loose collection of files that is spread to multiple locations and is interconnected by a network.
A single logical database that is limited to one location.
A loose collection of files that is limited to one location.
questions.explanation: A distributed database is a single logical database that is physically spread across multiple locations connected by a network.

questions.question: Which of the following is the oldest database model?
questions.explanation: The hierarchical database model was the earliest database model, developed in the 1960s with the IBM Information Management System (IMS).

questions.question: Procedural language among the following is ____.
questions.explanation: Relational algebra is a procedural query language where operations are specified in a step-by-step manner.

questions.question: Which type of data can be stored in the database?
options: Data in the form of audio or video
questions.explanation: Modern databases can store various data types including images, text files, audio, and video content.

questions.question: A transaction goes into a(n) ____ state immediately after it starts execution where it can issue read or write operations.
questions.explanation: After a transaction starts, it enters the Active state where it can perform read and write operations.

questions.question: ____ is Potential Problems Caused By Concurrency which occurs when a transaction reads several values from the database but a second transaction updates some of them during the execution of the first.
questions.explanation: The inconsistent analysis problem occurs when a transaction reads data while another transaction is updating it, leading to inconsistent aggregate calculations.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true about handling of deadlock.
options: If the probability of deadlocks is low > deadlock detection,
If the probability of deadlocks is high > deadlock prevention.
If response time is not high on the system's priority list > deadlock avoidance.
questions.explanation: All statements correctly describe deadlock handling strategies: detection for low probability, prevention for high probability, and avoidance when response time is not critical.

questions.question: In ARIES recovery Algorithm which phase is determine Undo transaction.
questions.explanation: The Undo pass in ARIES recovery algorithm determines which transactions need to be rolled back (undone) and performs the actual undo operations.

questions.question: Which one of the following is false about TCP and UDP?
options: TCP is guaranteed delivery, UDP is not guaranteed.
TCP guarantees order of messages, UDP doesn't.
TCP is slower compared to UDP
TCP uses Port number, but UDP does not
questions.explanation: This statement is false because both TCP and UDP use port numbers for identifying applications. TCP provides connection-oriented, reliable communication while UDP is connectionless.

questions.question: Which one of the following is false about Servlet?
options: A servlet program to be executed it needs a web server with servlet engine
A servlet is a server side script that provide a dynamic nature of a web
A servlet is portable among operating systems
A servlet can handle multiple requests concurrently
questions.explanation: All statements about servlets are true. Servlets require a web server with a servlet engine, provide dynamic web content, are portable across operating systems, and can handle multiple concurrent requests.

questions.question: Which is multithreaded programming?
options: It's a process in which two different processes run simultaneously
It's a process in which two or more parts of same process run simultaneously
It's a process in which many different process are able to access same information
It's a process in which a single process can access information from many sources
questions.explanation: Multithreaded programming involves multiple threads (parts) of the same process running concurrently, sharing the process's resources but executing independently.

questions.question: The client and server communication on top of TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) have the following unordered steps. Hence, which one of the following is the correct order of these steps? i. The server wait and accept for the client incoming connection request ii. The client and server perform communication dialog iii. The server create a socket at specified port for incoming connection request iv. The server and client close the socket connection v. The client create a socket at specified server IP address and port number for connection request
questions.explanation: The correct order is: Server creates socket (iii) -> Server waits for connection (i) -> Client creates socket (v) -> Communication dialog (ii) -> Close connection (iv).

questions.question: Select all the incorrect statements about HashSet and LinkedHashSet
options: HashSet does not maintain the insertion order of the elements
LinkedHashSet maintains the ordering of the elements and guarantees insertion order
HashSet does not necessarily maintain the insertion order of the elements
HashSet and LinkedHashSet are the implementing classes of the Set interface
HashSet and LinkedHashSet are the implementing classes of the SortedSet interface
questions.explanation: HashSet and LinkedHashSet implement the Set interface, not the SortedSet interface. SortedSet is implemented by TreeSet.

questions.question: Select the valid thread state transition?
questions.explanation: Ready to running is a valid state transition where a thread that is ready to run is selected by the scheduler to actually run on the CPU.

questions.question: Which tag is used to execute java source code in JSP?
questions.explanation: The Scriptlet tag (<% ... %>) is used to embed Java code in JSP pages for execution when the page is requested.

questions.question: Which of these is synchronized?
questions.explanation: Hashtable is synchronized (thread-safe) by default, while TreeMap and HashMap are not synchronized.

questions.question: When we implement the servlet program in java, which method is mandatory to define the body command after overriding?
questions.explanation: When implementing a servlet, you must override at least one of the doGet(), doPost(), or service() methods to handle client requests.

questions.question: Which java package is used to implement the network based systems?
questions.explanation: The java.net package provides classes for networking functionality, including sockets, URLs, and network communication.

questions.question: In java, an IP address is defined as an object, the instance of class ____.
questions.explanation: InetAddress is the Java class that represents an IP address, with subclasses Inet4Address and Inet6Address for IPv4 and IPv6 respectively.

questions.question: The client in socket programming based on TCP protocol must know which information?
options: Both IP address of Server and port number
questions.explanation: A TCP client must know both the server's IP address and port number to establish a connection to the server.

questions.question: A types of JDBC statement which is responsible for executing a database stored procedure ____.
questions.explanation: CallableStatement is used to execute stored procedures in the database. It provides methods for handling input and output parameters.

questions.question: A servlet implementation technique that can be used with any protocol ____.
questions.explanation: GenericServlet is protocol-independent and can be extended to support any protocol, unlike HttpServlet which is specific to HTTP.

questions.question: Which one is the correct order of phases in JSP life cycle?
questions.explanation: The JSP lifecycle consists of: Compilation (JSP to Servlet), Initialization, Execution (service method), and Cleanup (destroy).

questions.question: Which of the following is true about JSP? 1. JSP technology is used to create web application 2. The JSP pages are not easier to maintain than servlet 3. JSP page consists of HTML tags and JSP tags
questions.explanation: JSP is used for web applications and consists of HTML and JSP tags. Statement 2 is false because JSP pages are generally easier to maintain than servlets.

questions.question: Which of the following is false about Set interface java collection
options: A Set collection can contain duplicate elements
A Set collection cannot maintain element order
A Set object can be instantiated from HashSet sub-class
A Set object can be instantiated from TreeSet sub-class
questions.explanation: The Set interface does not allow duplicate elements. This statement is false because a Set cannot contain duplicate elements.

questions.question: Which types of IO stream is used to perform read based communication on top of TCP protocol
questions.explanation: DataInputStream is used to read data from a network connection over TCP, allowing reading of primitive data types in a portable way.

questions.question: Which collection interface restricts duplicate elements?
questions.explanation: Set interface restricts duplicate elements by design. List allows duplicates, and Map requires unique keys but may have duplicate values.

questions.question: Which one of the following is false about the java servlet life cycle?
options: In servlet init() method will be called only once during the lifetime of the servlet
The service() method will be called only once during the life time of the servlet
The destroy() method is called once when the servlet is being removed
The servlet is loaded by the container before initialization
questions.explanation: The service() method is called for each request, not just once. The init() method is called once and destroy() is called once.

questions.question: The ASP and JSP technologies are quite similar in the way they support the creation of Dynamic pages, using HTML templates, scripting code and components for business logic.
questions.explanation: ASP and JSP are both server-side technologies that create dynamic web pages using HTML templates, scripting code, and business logic components.

questions.question: Which of the following is true about List interface java collection?
options: a List collection can contain duplicate elements
a List collection cannot maintain element order
a List object can be instantiated from ArrayList sub-class
a List does not support item synchronization
questions.explanation: List collections allow duplicate elements by design. They maintain insertion order and can be instantiated using ArrayList or LinkedList implementations.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not true about client server communication on top of User Datagram Protocol?
options: A message is transferred from source machine to destination based on information contained that packet
Destination address is accessed from established socket
Packets may arrive to the destination in any order
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless, so there is no established socket connection. Each packet must contain destination address information for delivery.

questions.question: Assume in Wachemo University there are 1000 Instructor academic staffs and this year government increase their salary based on their academic position. Hence, based on this case study answer below questions (i) and (ii)
questions.explanation: PreparedStatement is most efficient and effective for executing UPDATE statements with parameters, as it pre-compiles the SQL and prevents SQL injection.

questions.question: Based on Question No. 24, which method is not able to execute the above sql statement (update statement)
questions.explanation: executeQuery() is designed for SELECT statements that return a ResultSet. It cannot be used for UPDATE statements. executeUpdate() and execute() can be used.

questions.question: Which one of the following is false about GET and POST request methods?
options: POST method is designed for posting information to the server
POST method used for large parametrized requests and larger forms
The doGet() method is the corresponding method for POST request
questions.explanation: doGet() corresponds to GET requests, not POST. doPost() is the corresponding method for POST requests. The other statements are true.

questions.question: JSPs eventually are compiled into Java servlets, you can do as much with JSPs as you can do with Java servlets.
questions.explanation: JSP pages are compiled into Java servlets by the container, so they can achieve the same functionality as servlets.

questions.question: What is the output of the following program? public class Question_7_1 { public static void main(String[] args) { ArrayDeque<Integer> deque = new ArrayDeque<Integer>(); deque.push(1); deque.push(2); deque.push(3);
questions.explanation: The ArrayDeque push() method adds elements to the front of the deque (like stack). With pushes of 1, 2, 3, the deque will contain [1, 2, 3].

questions.question: Which one of the following is not true about ResultSet in JDBC?
options: ResultSet is a logical view of row and column data of the actual database that meets the criteria of requested SQL query
The SQL statement executor function execute() of statement object may return a ResultSet
Despite the number of rows in a result set return from manipulated query, at a time only one row is accessible
To access the values of fields in database from ResultSet possible to use either columnIndex or columnName
questions.explanation: All statements about ResultSet are true. ResultSet provides access to query results, execute() can return ResultSet, rows are accessed one at a time, and values can be accessed by index or name.

questions.question: Which of the following are the advantages of Java Servlet over the other common server extensions?
options: Java servlets are faster than other server extensions like CGI scripts.
Java servlets use a standard API that is supported by many browsers.
Java servlets are portable between server and operating system.
questions.explanation: Servlets offer multiple advantages including faster performance than CGI, standard API support, and portability across servers and operating systems.

questions.question: Which of the following are the valid scopes in JSP?
questions.explanation: Valid JSP scopes are request, page, session, and application. 'global' and 'context' are not valid JSP scope names.

questions.question: Which types of IO stream is used to perform read based communication on top of TCP protocol
questions.explanation: DataInputStream is used for reading data from a TCP connection, allowing primitive data types to be read in a platform-independent way.

questions.question: The life cycle method of a servlet which is responsible for handling all incoming requests from the client side
questions.explanation: The service() method is responsible for handling all incoming client requests. It determines the request type (GET, POST, etc.) and delegates appropriately.

questions.question: The ____ class is used to create datagram packets.
questions.explanation: DatagramPacket class is used to create datagram packets for UDP communication. DatagramSocket is used for sending and receiving these packets.

questions.question: A Map can contain duplicate keys
questions.explanation: This is false. Map interfaces do not allow duplicate keys. Each key can map to at most one value.

questions.question: Which method is called internally by Thread start() method?
questions.explanation: The start() method internally calls the run() method of the thread. The run() method contains the code that executes in the new thread.

questions.question: Which of the following object of java.sql package is responsible to manage the registering and unregistering of database drivers from underlying system.
questions.explanation: DriverManager is responsible for managing database drivers, including registering and unregistering them from the system.

questions.question: Which collection class maintains insertion order?
questions.explanation: ArrayList maintains insertion order. TreeSet and HashSet do not maintain insertion order (they maintain sorted order or no specific order).

questions.question: Which method will contain the body of the thread in Java?
questions.explanation: The run() method contains the code that is executed when the thread is started. This is the body of the thread.

questions.question: Which one of the following is false about client server communication on top of User Datagram Protocol?
options: A message is transferred from source machine to destination based on information contained that packet
Destination address is accessed from established socket
Packets may arrive to the destination in any order
questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless, so there is no established socket connection from which to access destination address. Each packet contains complete destination information.

questions.question: The steps given below are a set of unordered activities used in java database connectivity in any underlying system. Hence, write the correct order of these activities based on their label: a. Establish the Connection b. Execute a query c. Load the JDBC driver d. Create a Statement object e. Process the results f. Define the Connection URL g. Close the connection
questions.explanation: The correct JDBC sequence is: Load driver (c) -> Define URL (f) -> Establish Connection (a) -> Create Statement (d) -> Execute Query (b) -> Process Results (e) -> Close Connection (g).

questions.question: Which interface provides key-value pair?
questions.explanation: Map interface provides key-value pair storage, where each key is associated with a value. List and Set store single elements, Collection is a root interface.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true about port number and IP address?
options: Port number is an identification given for computer machines
IP address is an identification given for servers with in a machine
Only IP address is required to establish TCP based client server communication
Port number is represented in dotted quad format
questions.explanation: None of the statements are true. IP addresses identify machines, ports identify applications/processes on a machine, both are needed for TCP communication, and IP addresses use dotted quad format.

questions.question: Which Interface does not allow duplicates?
questions.explanation: Set interface does not allow duplicate elements. List allows duplicates, and Map requires unique keys but may have duplicate values.

questions.question: Which one of the following not true about TCP protocol?
options: It stands for Transmission Control Protocol
It is connection oriented types of protocol
It does not allow reliable communication between two applications
It provides flow control and error recovery
questions.explanation: TCP does provide reliable communication between two applications. The other statements are true: it is connection-oriented and provides flow control and error recovery.

questions.question: Which of these is synchronized?
questions.explanation: Vector is synchronized by default. ArrayList and LinkedList are not synchronized (thread-safe).

questions.question: Which of these maintains insertion order?
questions.explanation: List maintains insertion order by default. Set does not maintain insertion order generally (except LinkedHashSet).

questions.question: Which class is responsible for managing the loading and unloading of database drivers from the underlying system
questions.explanation: DriverManager is responsible for managing database drivers, including loading and unloading them from the system.

questions.question: What is maximum thread priority in Java
questions.explanation: The maximum thread priority in Java is 10 (MAX_PRIORITY). The priority values range from 1 (MIN_PRIORITY) to 10 (MAX_PRIORITY).

questions.question: _____ Is when the computer is turned on and the operating system is loading.
questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting a computer and loading the operating system. It involves power-on self-test and loading the OS into memory.

questions.question: _____ is a situation when a program misbehaves only when certain conditions met otherwise it works as a genuine program.
questions.explanation: A logic bomb is a malicious program that triggers only when specific conditions are met, behaving normally otherwise. It's a type of malware that stays dormant until triggered.

questions.question: What is Trojan horse?
options: It is a useful way to encrypt password
It is a user which steals valuable information
It is a rogue program which tricks users
It's a brute force attack algorithm
questions.explanation: A Trojan horse is a malicious program that disguises itself as legitimate software to trick users into installing it. It performs malicious actions without the user's knowledge.

questions.question: When you delete a file in your computer, where does it go?
questions.explanation: When a file is deleted in Windows, it's moved to the Recycle Bin, where it can be restored if needed before permanent deletion.

questions.question: Which program runs first after booting the computer and loading the GUI?
questions.explanation: Windows Explorer is the first program that runs after booting, providing the graphical user interface, taskbar, and file management functionality.

questions.question: One is show that the software related problem (select more best answers)
questions.explanation: Multiple software-related problems include corrupt registry, improper drivers, viruses, and compatibility errors. Thrashing is typically a hardware/performance issue.

questions.question: What is Microsoft window?
questions.explanation: Microsoft Windows is an operating system that provides a graphical user interface and manages computer hardware and software resources.

questions.question: Which is the first program run on a computer when the computer boots up?
questions.explanation: The operating system is the first program loaded during boot process, which then manages other software and hardware components.

questions.question: Beep codes are generated by which of the following?
questions.explanation: POST (Power-On Self-Test) generates beep codes to indicate hardware issues during startup. Different beep patterns indicate different problems.

questions.question: Which bus slot provides the highest video performance?
questions.explanation: PCIe (Peripheral Component Interconnect Express) provides the highest video performance with faster data transfer rates compared to PCI, SCSI, and AGP.

questions.question: Which of the following connectors is used for musical equipment?
questions.explanation: MIDI (Musical Instrument Digital Interface) is a protocol and connector standard specifically designed for musical equipment and instruments.

questions.question: Moving your CPU's speed beyond its normal operating range is called
questions.explanation: Overclocking is the practice of running a CPU at higher clock speeds than specified by the manufacturer, potentially improving performance but risking stability and heat issues.

questions.question: Which password is used in the BIOS (CMOS) to prevent end users from accessing the BIOS contents?
questions.explanation: Supervisor (or Administrator) password in BIOS prevents unauthorized users from changing BIOS settings. User password restricts system boot access.

questions.question: What does a yellow exclamation point next to a device in the Device Manager indicate?
options: A driver is not properly installed for this device.
The driver is not digitally signed.
The device driver needs to be upgraded.
questions.explanation: A yellow exclamation mark in Device Manager indicates a device driver issue, usually meaning the driver is not properly installed or the device has a problem.

questions.question: Which tool should always be used when working on the inside of the computer?
questions.explanation: An antistatic strap (or ESD strap) should always be used to prevent electrostatic discharge from damaging sensitive computer components during internal work.

questions.question: On a laptop, which of the following would most likely be a pointing device?
questions.explanation: Touchpad is the most common integrated pointing device on laptops. External mice may be used but are not built-in.

questions.question: Which device can store a maximum of 1.44 MB on a removable disk?
questions.explanation: A standard 3.5-inch floppy disk drive stores up to 1.44 MB of data. CD-ROMs store much more (650-700 MB).

questions.question: Which type of RAM has a peak transfer of 12,800 MB/s?
questions.explanation: DDR3-1600 has a peak transfer rate of 12,800 MB/s (1600 MHz × 8 bytes per transfer). DDR2-1600 has 12,800 MB/s but is less common.

questions.question: A computer you are working on has a lot of dust inside it. How should you clean this?
options: Disassemble the power supply and remove the dust.
Use a vacuum to clean up the dust.
Use a surface dust cleaning solution.
Use compressed air to remove the dust.
questions.explanation: Compressed air is the safest method for cleaning dust from computer components. Vacuums can create static electricity, and solutions/liquids can damage electronics.

questions.question: Setting an administrator password in the BIOS accomplishes which of the following?
options: Prevents a user from rearranging the boot order
Prevents a user from reading e-mail
Prevents a virus from infecting the MBR
Prevents an attacker from opening the case
questions.explanation: BIOS administrator password prevents unauthorized users from changing BIOS settings, including boot order. It doesn't affect email reading, MBR infection, or physical case access.

questions.question: What is an LCD display's contrast ratio defined as?
questions.explanation: Contrast ratio is the difference between the brightest white and the darkest black the display can produce, expressed as a ratio (e.g., 1000:1).

questions.question: Which of the following tools can protect you in the case of a surge?
questions.explanation: An antistatic mat provides protection against electrical surges by safely dissipating static electricity. It grounds the user and components.

questions.question: What connector can have audio and video pass through it?
questions.explanation: HDMI (High-Definition Multimedia Interface) can carry both audio and video signals. VGA, RGB, and DVI typically only carry video signals.

questions.question: You just upgraded the CPU. Which of the following can make your computer shut down automatically after a few minutes? (Select the best answer.)
questions.explanation: CPU overheating triggers thermal protection mechanisms that cause automatic shutdown. This is common after CPU upgrades with improper cooling.

questions.question: Which of the following power connections might be used by hard drives? (Select the two best answers.)
questions.explanation: Hard drives typically use Molex (4-pin) or Berg (4-pin) power connectors. Modern SATA drives use different connectors, but these are common for legacy/IDE drives.

questions.question: You want to upgrade memory in your computer. Which of the following is user-replaceable memory in a PC?
questions.explanation: DRAM (Dynamic RAM) is the main system memory that users can upgrade by adding or replacing memory modules. BIOS/CMOS are on chips and ROM is permanent.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a configuration that can be made in the BIOS?
questions.explanation: Installing drivers is an operating system function, not a BIOS configuration. BIOS can configure boot sequence, temperature monitoring, overclocking, and intrusion detection.

questions.question: When working on a computer, which of the following should you disconnect to prevent electrical shock? (Select the two best answers.)
questions.explanation: Disconnecting the power supply cord and power cord is essential to prevent electrical shock. Printers and mice don't carry dangerous voltages.

questions.question: Which of the following controls the connection between the CPU and the PCIe x16 expansion slot?
questions.explanation: The Northbridge chipset manages communication between the CPU and high-speed components like PCIe slots, memory, and graphics cards.

questions.question: A customer experiences a server crash. When you arrive, the manager is upset about this problem. What should you do in this scenario?
options: Stay calm and do the job as efficiently as possible.
Take the customer out for a cup of coffee.
Avoid the customer and get the job done quickly.
Refer the customer to your supervisor.
questions.explanation: The best approach is to remain professional and calm, focus on solving the problem efficiently while being respectful to the upset customer.

questions.question: As you are servicing a manager's PC at your company, you run across a list of names of employees who are supposedly about to be let go from the company. Some of these people are coworkers. What should you do?
options: Act as if you never saw the list.
In secret, tell everyone who was on the list.
Yell at the manager for having that list out.
questions.explanation: The professional approach is to act as if you never saw confidential information and maintain confidentiality. Sharing it would be unethical and could get you fired.

questions.question: Which of the following is the newest type of mouse connection?
questions.explanation: USB (Universal Serial Bus) is the newest and most common mouse connection type, replacing older serial and PS/2 connections.

questions.question: Which of the following is a unique characteristic of a dual-core processor versus a single-core processor?
options: A dual-core processor has two cores, with separate caches, on the same physical chip.
A dual-core processor has several unique cores, with the same cache, on two different chips.
A dual-core processor uses higher voltage than a single-core processor.
A dual-core processor requires more RAM to function than a single-core processor.
questions.explanation: Dual-core processors have two independent cores on a single chip with separate caches, allowing parallel processing while sharing other resources.

questions.question: You need to expand the peripherals of a computer, but the system doesn't have enough ports. Which type of card should you install?
questions.explanation: A USB expansion card adds additional USB ports to the system, allowing more peripherals to be connected to the computer.

questions.question: Which of the following is a typical speed of a SATA hard drive?
questions.explanation: 7200 RPM is a typical rotational speed for SATA hard drives. Mbps refers to network speed, GHz to processor speed, and GB to storage capacity.

questions.question: One way to provide preventive maintenance to a hard drive is to do what?
options: Upgrade the cache on the drive to improve performance.
Increase the amount of RAM on the PC to increase the page file.
Keep an area of airflow around the drive so that it doesn't overheat.
questions.explanation: Proper airflow prevents hard drive overheating, which is a common cause of drive failure. Good cooling is an important preventive maintenance measure.

questions.question: A USB port can connect up to ____ different peripherals together with a single connector.
questions.explanation: A single USB port can connect up to 127 peripherals through hubs, limited by the USB specification's addressable device count.

questions.question: You need to replace and upgrade the memory card in a smartphone. Which type of memory does this smartphone most likely use?
questions.explanation: Smartphones typically use SD (Secure Digital) memory cards or microSD cards for expandable storage. CF cards are larger and used in professional cameras.

questions.question: Assume that you are computer technician in the Wachemo University ICT Department, you receive the following customer request from different departments. Based on the client request you have, which order the client request service is more correct from high to low priority request based on the organization critical system? 1) Mr. Abera from Management Department request to his computer always restart 2) Dr. Multa from Physics Department request his computer is show black screen 3) Dr. Abebe from Human resource office request as you develop new software resource 4) Mr. Abera from Worldbright college request you his monitor do not work 5) Mr. Geda from civil Engineering Department request you his computer giving warning for disk full 6) Miss. Abeba from HR department her computer program which is used to calculate employees salary do not work
questions.explanation: The correct priority order should prioritize critical business systems: payroll system failure (6), new software needs (3), display issues (4), disk warnings (5), restarting computers (1), and black screens (2).

questions.question: Which software used to make bootable USB driver for windows 10
questions.explanation: All these tools (Power ISO, Rufus, USB installer) can create bootable USB drives for Windows 10 installation. Rufus is particularly popular and effective.

questions.question: What are the basic idea we consider during we formatting the computer? (select any best answer(s))
options: Check the minimum HW requirement of the windows you have
Make the bootable devices such as USB Driver
Identify the partition of your driver
questions.explanation: All factors are important: checking hardware requirements, preparing bootable media, backing up data, and understanding partition structure before formatting.

questions.question: Which software is called as product oriented software
questions.explanation: Application software is product-oriented, designed to perform specific tasks for end users. System software manages computer resources.

questions.question: Which types of system software used to manage processor, Memory, files and protecting as well as scheduling the computer program
questions.explanation: The operating system manages hardware resources including processor, memory, files, and scheduling, providing a foundation for other software.

questions.question: The system software which is used to manage particular types of hardware devices that attached to the computer such as printer, keyboard and network is called
questions.explanation: Device drivers are specialized software that manage specific hardware devices, providing a communication interface between the OS and hardware.

questions.question: The types of system software that make computer work more efficiently or boast the performance of the computer is known as
questions.explanation: System utility software enhances system performance through optimization, disk cleanup, defragmentation, and other maintenance tasks.

questions.question: Select the correct statement about the abstract view of the components of a computer system with the system software
options: The placement of the operating system is at the bottom of is the driver software
In the computer system On the top of the hardware is always the driver software
Utility software acts as an intermediary between the user of a computer and the computer hardware
Driver system is used to hides the hardware and gives the programmer a more convenient set of instructions to work with.
questions.explanation: Device drivers abstract the hardware details and provide a standardized interface, making it easier for programmers to interact with hardware devices.

questions.question: From the following software which is the language software
questions.explanation: Compiler software is language software that translates high-level programming code into machine code. It's a type of language processing software.

questions.question: From the following software types which one is used to change high level language to low level statement by statement ...
questions.explanation: An interpreter translates high-level language statements line-by-line during execution, unlike a compiler which translates the entire program at once.

questions.question: Which types of operating system does not allows as user and computer does not interact directly
questions.explanation: Batch operating systems process jobs in batches without user interaction. Users submit jobs and receive results later without direct system interaction.

questions.question: Which types of operating system provide the environment in which multiple independent computer work to each other
questions.explanation: Distributed operating systems manage multiple independent computers as a single system, allowing them to work together and share resources.

questions.question: The network of electric wire inside the computer system which allow as the components communicate to each other is known as
questions.explanation: A bus is a communication system that transfers data between components inside a computer, allowing them to communicate with each other.

questions.question: The data bus is ____ directional.
questions.explanation: The data bus is bidirectional, allowing data to flow in both directions between components, enabling both read and write operations.

questions.question: A program in execution is called a
questions.explanation: A program in execution is called a process. A process includes the program code, its current activity, and the execution context.

questions.question: Which is not an example of a peripheral device?
questions.explanation: A register is an internal CPU component, not a peripheral device. Peripherals are external devices connected to the computer.

questions.question: The speed at which a CPU processes data to convert it, is measured in:
questions.explanation: CPU processing speed is measured in hertz (usually gigahertz or MHz), representing the number of clock cycles per second. Megabytes/Gigabytes/Terabytes measure storage.

questions.question: For each instructions of program in memory the CPU goes through a
questions.explanation: The CPU executes instructions through the fetch-decode-execute cycle: fetches the instruction from memory, decodes it, then executes the operation.

questions.question: Which memory is non volatile and may be written only once.
questions.explanation: PROM (Programmable Read-Only Memory) is non-volatile and can be programmed only once. RAM is volatile, EPROM can be erased with UV light, and EEPROM can be electrically erased.

questions.question: In magnetic disks data is organized on the platter in a concentric sets or rings called
questions.explanation: Tracks are concentric rings on the disk platter where data is stored. Sectors are subdivisions of tracks, and heads read/write data.

questions.question: which file system is allow the permission, encryption and compression on the file
questions.explanation: NTFS (New Technology File System) supports advanced features including file permissions, encryption, and compression. FAT file systems lack these features.

questions.question: ____ is an operating system's overall structure in which file named, stored and organized in the storage devices.
questions.explanation: A file system is the structure that organizes and manages files on storage devices, including naming, storing, and organizing data.

questions.question: ____ is the process of creating logical division of the hard driver in one or more.
questions.explanation: Partitioning creates logical divisions on a physical hard drive, allowing it to be divided into separate sections that can be used independently.

questions.question: ____ is the process of creating and configuring a file allocation table or new technology file system as well as creating the root directory ...
questions.explanation: Formatting creates the file system structure (FAT or NTFS) and root directory on a partition, preparing it for data storage.

questions.question: From the following file system types which one is the oldest version file allocation types
questions.explanation: FAT12 is the oldest version of the File Allocation Table system, dating back to the early 1980s. FAT16, FAT32, and exFAT are later improvements.

questions.question: From the following file Allocation table which one have maximum number of clusters
questions.explanation: exFAT supports the maximum number of clusters (up to 2^32) among these options, making it suitable for large drives. FAT32 supports fewer clusters.

questions.question: Which one of the following is false about the New Technology file system on the storage devices
options: It is automatically repair the hard driver error without displaying the error message
It keep the detail about the transaction log which help to recover file from failure
It supports file compression and encryption
It supports file permissions and quotas
questions.explanation: NTFS does not automatically repair hard drive errors without notification. While it supports error logging and recovery, errors are typically reported to the user.

questions.question: In comparison to the internal (main) memory, tape or disk memory is
questions.explanation: Tape and disk memory are slower and less expensive than internal (main) memory, making them suitable for long-term storage and backups.

questions.question: Arithmetic logic unit I. perform arithmetic operations II. store data III. perform comparison IV. Communicate with input devices of the above the correct one is
questions.explanation: The ALU performs arithmetic operations and comparisons. Data storage and input/output communication are handled by other components (memory and I/O controllers).

questions.question: Impact printers
options: strike a ribbon against the paper to produce character images.
are more expensive than laser printers
questions.explanation: Impact printers work by striking an inked ribbon against paper to produce characters, similar to typewriters. Ink-jet and thermal printers are non-impact printers.

questions.question: Software is defined as
options: set of programs, documentation & configuration of data
questions.explanation: Software includes not only programs but also documentation and configuration data that support the program's operation and use.

questions.question: What is Software Engineering?
options: Application of engineering principles to the design a software
questions.explanation: Software Engineering applies systematic engineering principles to the design, development, and maintenance of software, not just coding or testing.

questions.question: What are the features of Software Code?
questions.explanation: Good software code features include simplicity, accessibility, and modularity - all characteristics of well-designed and maintainable code.

questions.question: ____ is a software development activity that is not a part of software processes.
questions.explanation: Dependence is not typically considered a software process activity. Core activities are specification, development, validation, and evolution.

questions.question: Define agile scrum methodology.
options: project management that emphasizes incremental progress
project management that emphasizes decremental progress
project management that emphasizes neutral progress
project management that emphasizes no progress
questions.explanation: Agile Scrum emphasizes incremental progress through sprints, delivering working software in small, manageable increments.

questions.question: ____ is defined as the process of generating analysis and designing documents?
questions.explanation: Reverse engineering is the process of analyzing software to create representations in higher levels of abstraction (analysis/design documents).

questions.question: What is a Functional Requirement?
options: specifies the tasks the program must complete
Specifies the tasks the program should not complete
Specifies the tasks the program must not work
questions.explanation: Functional requirements specify what the system must do - the tasks, functions, and behaviors the software must perform.

questions.question: Attributes of good software is
questions.explanation: Good software must be both functional and maintainable. Development is the process, not an attribute of the software itself.

questions.question: Regardless of application area, project size, or complexity, software development work may be divided into three generic phases: the ____ phase, which focuses on what, the ____ phase, which focuses on how, and the ____ phase, which focuses on change.
questions.explanation: The three generic software development phases are definition (what), development (how), and support (change/maintenance).

questions.question: ____ is a software development life cycle model that is chosen if the development team has less experience on similar projects.
questions.explanation: The Spiral model is chosen when the team has less experience as it emphasizes risk analysis and iterative development, allowing learning and adaptation.

questions.question: ____ is not suitable for accommodating any change?
questions.explanation: The Waterfall model is not suitable for accommodating changes as it follows a sequential approach where changes become difficult and expensive to implement.

questions.question: The model which has a major disadvantage in terms of the coding phase of a software life cycle model is
questions.explanation: The 4GT (Fourth Generation Techniques) model has disadvantages in coding as it automates code generation but lacks control and understanding of the generated code.

questions.question: What is the full form of the 'COCOMO' model?
questions.explanation: COCOMO stands for Constructive Cost Estimation Model, a widely used software cost estimation model developed by Barry Boehm.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not a software process quality?
questions.explanation: Portability is a software product quality characteristic, not a process quality characteristic. Process qualities include visibility, timeliness, and productivity.

questions.question: CLR is the .NET equivalent of
questions.explanation: CLR (Common Language Runtime) is Microsoft's equivalent to Java Virtual Machine, providing the runtime environment for .NET programs.

questions.question: The CLR is physically represented by an assembly named
questions.explanation: mscoree.dll is the main DLL that implements the Common Language Runtime. It contains the code for loading and executing .NET applications.

questions.question: The ____ language allows more than one method in a single class.
questions.explanation: C# allows method overloading, enabling multiple methods with the same name but different parameters in a single class.

questions.question: All C# applications begin execution by calling the ____ method.
questions.explanation: All C# applications start execution at the Main() method, which is the entry point of the application.

questions.question: A structure in C# provides a unique way of packing together data of ____ types.
questions.explanation: A structure in C# can pack together data of different types into a single data structure, similar to classes but as value types.

questions.question: Which of the following statements is correct about Managed Code?
options: Managed code is the code that runs on top of Windows.
Managed code is the code that is written to target the services of the CLR.
Managed code is the code where resources are Garbage Collected.
Managed code is the code that is compiled by the JIT compilers.
questions.explanation: Managed code is written to target the services of the CLR, which provides memory management, security, and exception handling services.

questions.question: C# runs on the
questions.explanation: C# primarily runs on the .NET Framework. It's not designed to run on Java Virtual Machine directly (though alternatives like IKVM exist).

questions.question: C# programming language is used to develop -
questions.explanation: C# is a versatile language used for developing web applications (ASP.NET), desktop applications (Windows Forms, WPF), and mobile apps (Xamarin).

questions.question: Who is the founder of C# programming language?
questions.explanation: Anders Hejlsberg is the principal designer of C#, leading the development team at Microsoft. He also designed Turbo Pascal and was a key developer of Delphi.

questions.question: CLR stands for
questions.explanation: CLR stands for Common Language Runtime, which provides the execution environment for .NET applications.

questions.question: Net CLR is equivalent to?
questions.explanation: The .NET CLR is equivalent to Java Virtual Machine (JVM) - both provide runtime environments for their respective platforms.

questions.question: What is CLR in C#?
options: It is a virtual machine component of Microsoft .NET Framework
It is a virtual machine component of JVM
It is a compiler to compiler the C# code
questions.explanation: CLR is a virtual machine component of Microsoft .NET Framework that manages code execution, security, and memory management.

questions.question: What does the CLR in C# do?
options: Manages the execution of Webpages programs
Manages the parsing of the various types
questions.explanation: CLR manages the execution of .NET programs, handling memory allocation, garbage collection, security, and thread management.

questions.question: SOAP in C# stands for
questions.explanation: SOAP stands for Simple Object Access Protocol, a protocol used for exchanging structured information in web services.

questions.question: Garbage collection automatically reclaims memory occupied by unreachable unused objects. - This statement is true or false in C#?
questions.explanation: This is true. C# automatically manages memory through garbage collection, which identifies and reclaims unused memory.

questions.question: Which symbols are used to mark the beginning and end of a code block?
questions.explanation: Curly braces {} mark the beginning and end of code blocks in C#, including method bodies, class definitions, and control flow statements.

questions.question: Every C# statement is terminated by
questions.explanation: Every C# statement ends with a semicolon (;), except for statements that define blocks (like method declarations or class definitions).

questions.question: In C#, a single-line comment starts with
questions.explanation: Single-line comments in C# start with two forward slashes (//). Everything after // on that line is a comment.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax to declare a variable in C#?
questions.explanation: Variables can be declared with or without initialization: 'type variableName;' or 'type variableName = value;'. Both are valid C# syntax.

questions.question: Which data type is used to store text value in C#?
questions.explanation: The string data type is used to store text in C#. 'string' is an alias for System.String class.

questions.question: Which C# keyword is used to define a constant?
questions.explanation: The 'const' keyword is used to define constants in C#, which are values that cannot be changed during program execution.

questions.question: What is the correct syntax to define a C# constant?
questions.explanation: Constants must be assigned a value at compile time. Syntax: 'const type constantName = value;'

questions.question: What is the C# keyword which is used to change data and behaviour of a base class by replacing a member of the base class with a new derived member?
questions.explanation: The 'new' keyword is used to explicitly hide a member inherited from a base class, effectively changing the behavior in the derived class.

questions.question: How many catch blocks can be used with a single try block in C#?
questions.explanation: A single try block can have multiple catch blocks to handle different types of exceptions specifically.

questions.question: Event-driven languages are:
options: Are used to write procedural languages
Designed to make programming GUI easier
questions.explanation: Event-driven languages like C# and Java are designed to make GUI programming easier by responding to user interactions and system events.

questions.question: What does the CLR in C# do?
options: Manages the execution of Webpages programs
Manages the parsing of the various types
questions.explanation: CLR manages the execution of .NET programs, handling memory allocation, garbage collection, security, and thread management.

questions.question: In C#, the multi-line comments placed within the
questions.explanation: Multi-line comments in C# are placed between /* and */, allowing comments to span multiple lines.

questions.question: Which is the correct order for explicit type conversion to convert a larger to a smaller type in C#?
options: double => float => long => int => char => bool
float => double => long => int => char => bool
questions.explanation: The order from larger to smaller type for explicit conversion is: double -> float -> long -> int -> char. bool cannot be converted from these types.

questions.question: Which is the correct C# statement to convert a float value to int explicitly?
questions.explanation: The correct syntax for explicit conversion is '(int)float_variable'. The parentheses are required for the cast operator.

questions.question: Which is/are the correct method(s) to input a float value in C#?
questions.explanation: Both Parse(Console.ReadLine()) and ToSingle(Console.ReadLine()) can convert string input to float. ToFloat is not a valid method in C#.

questions.question: In C#, structures are used for ____ objects such as mobiles, cars, etc.
questions.explanation: Structures in C# are lightweight objects used for simple data containers, like representing small objects such as mobiles, cars, etc.

questions.question: What is the first step in project planning?
questions.explanation: Establishing objectives and scope is the first step in project planning, defining what the project aims to achieve and its boundaries.

questions.question: Which from the following represents the correct project cycle?
questions.explanation: The correct project cycle is: Initiating (project charter), Planning (detailed plans), Executing (doing the work), and Closing (finalizing).

questions.question: Following is (are) the component(s) of risk management
questions.explanation: Risk management includes assessment (identifying risks), control (managing risks), and ranking (prioritizing risks).

questions.question: Controlling the changes in the project may affect
questions.explanation: Change control affects project progress, costs at different stages, and the project scope - all aspects of the project.

questions.question: Resources refers to
questions.explanation: Project resources include manpower (human resources), machinery (equipment), and materials needed for project execution.

questions.question: Which one of the following project cost management processes incorrectly match?
options: Resource planning: determining what resources and quantities of them should be used.
Cost estimating: developing an estimate of the costs and resources needed to complete a project.
Cost Control: allocating the overall cost estimate to individual work items to establish a baseline for measuring performance.
questions.explanation: Cost Control is the process of monitoring and controlling project costs, not allocating estimates. Cost budgeting is the process of allocating estimates to work items.

questions.question: ____ is a project performance measurement technique that integrates scope, time, and cost data?
questions.explanation: Earned Value Management (EVM) integrates scope, schedule, and cost data to provide project performance measurements.

questions.question: Which one of the following modern quality managements?
questions.explanation: Modern quality management requires customer focus, prefers prevention over inspection, and recognizes management responsibility for quality.

questions.question: ____ reducing the impact of a risk event by reducing the probability of its occurrence.
questions.explanation: Risk mitigation reduces the probability and/or impact of a risk event. Avoidance eliminates the risk, transfer shifts it, and acceptance acknowledges it.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not the Causes of Project Management Failure?
options: Adequate planning, assumptions, risks, or resources
Use of new or unproven technologies/methods
questions.explanation: Adequate planning is not a cause of failure - it actually prevents failure. The other options are known causes of project management failure.

questions.question: Which one of the following is mismatching project scope management processes?
options: Scope Planning—developing a written scope statement as the basis for future project decisions.
Scope Definition—subdividing the major project deliverables into smaller, more manageable components.
Scope Verification—controlling changes to project scope.
questions.explanation: Scope Verification is the process of formalizing acceptance of the project scope, not controlling changes. Scope Control handles changes.

questions.question: Which one of the following is mismatching about project risk management processes?
options: Risk identification: determining which risks are likely to affect a project.
Qualitative risk analysis: characterizing and analyzing risks and prioritizing their effects on project objectives
Quantitative risk analysis: measuring the probability and consequences of risks
Risk response planning: taking steps to enhance opportunities and reduce threats to meeting project objectives
questions.explanation: All listed processes correctly match with their descriptions in risk management. None are mismatched.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not the tool and techniques of quality control?
questions.explanation: Stakeholder Analysis is a project management tool, not specifically a quality control tool. Pareto analysis, control charts, and testing are quality tools.

questions.question: ____ defines the coverage area of a project and what part of the business is to be studied?
questions.explanation: Both system boundary and scope define the coverage area of a project and what part of the business will be studied.

questions.question: ____ defines strategies or implementation steps to attain the identified goals.
questions.explanation: Technical approach defines the strategies and implementation steps needed to achieve the identified goals and objectives.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not IT project?
options: A new reservation system developed for airlines
Enhance existing systems to perform many business functions
questions.explanation: Designing a new transportation vehicle is an engineering project, not an IT project. The other options involve information systems.

questions.question: Which one of the following may not cause of project failure?
questions.explanation: Adequate planning prevents project failure rather than causing it. Poor communication, scope creep, and resource issues are common causes of failure.

questions.question: Which one of the following is advantage of using formal project management principles?
questions.explanation: Better internal coordination is an advantage of formal project management. Lower cost or shorter time aren't guaranteed benefits.

questions.question: ____ is the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet project requirements?
questions.explanation: Project Management is defined as the application of knowledge, skills, tools, and techniques to project activities to meet project requirements.

questions.question: Which one of the following is incorrect about project plan attributes?
options: Plans should foremost guide project execution
Plans should be updated as changes occur
questions.explanation: Plans should not be static; they should be dynamic and updated as changes occur during the project lifecycle.

questions.question: ____ includes the processes involved in defining and controlling what is or is not included in the project.
questions.explanation: Project Scope Management plan includes processes for defining and controlling what is included in the project scope.

questions.question: One of the following may not include in scope planning and scope statement
options: A brief description of the project's products.
A summary of all project deliverables.
A statement of what determines project failure
questions.explanation: A statement of what determines project failure is not typically included in scope planning. Scope statements include justification, product description, and deliverables.

questions.question: ____ are the people involved in or affected by project activities and include the project sponsor, project manager, project team, users, suppliers, and even opponents of the project.
questions.explanation: Stakeholders are all people who are involved in or affected by the project, including sponsors, managers, team members, users, suppliers, and opponents.

questions.question: ____ includes the processes required to ensure that the various elements of the project are properly coordinated.
questions.explanation: Project Integration Management includes processes to coordinate various project elements and ensure proper integration.

questions.question: ____ involves identifying and documenting interactivity logical relationships or reviewing activities and determining dependencies.
questions.explanation: Activity sequencing involves identifying and documenting logical relationships and dependencies between project activities.

questions.question: ____ is a project network analysis technique used to predict total project duration.
options: Slack or Free Time or Float
questions.explanation: PERT (Program Evaluation and Review Technique) analysis predicts total project duration using optimistic, pessimistic, and most likely time estimates.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true about Schedule Control
options: Don't plan for everyone to work at 100% capacity all the time
Hold progress meetings with stakeholders and be clear and honest in communicating schedule issues.
questions.explanation: It's important not to plan for everyone to work at 100% capacity. This causes burnout and schedule slippage. Allow for contingencies and perform reality checks.

questions.question: Which one of the following is miss matching about Project Cost Management Processes
options: Cost estimating: determining what resources (people, equipment, materials) and quantities of them should be used.
Resource planning: developing an estimate of the costs and resources needed to complete a project.
Cost budgeting: allocating the overall cost estimate to individual work items to establish a baseline for measuring performance.
Cost control: controlling changes to the project budget.
questions.explanation: Cost estimating is for estimating costs, not determining resources. Resource planning determines what resources are needed. The descriptions for cost budgeting and control are correct.

questions.question: Project cost control includes
options: ensuring that only appropriate project changes are included in a revised cost baseline
informing project stakeholders of authorized changes to the project that will affect costs
questions.explanation: Cost control includes monitoring cost performance, ensuring appropriate changes affect the baseline, and informing stakeholders of cost-related changes.

questions.question: ____ includes all the activities related to satisfying the relevant quality standards for a project.
questions.explanation: Quality control includes all activities related to monitoring, verifying, and satisfying quality standards throughout the project.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not Cost of Quality category codes
questions.explanation: Measurement and test equipment costs are not typically considered a separate cost of quality category. The main categories are prevention, appraisal, and failure costs.

questions.question: Outputs and processes include
questions.explanation: All these are outputs and processes of project management - organizational charts, work definition, assignment processes, and RACI matrices.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not an identified influence bases that are available to project managers
questions.explanation: Motivation and effectiveness are outcomes of good management, not influence bases. The listed influence bases include authority, budget, money/penalty, and work challenge.

questions.question: ____ includes both enhancing the ability of stakeholders to contribute as individuals as well as enhancing the ability of the team to function as a team.
questions.explanation: Team development enhances individual contributions and team functioning, improving collaboration and project performance.

questions.question: ____ involves getting the needed human resources (individuals or groups) assigned to and working on the project.
questions.explanation: Staff acquisition involves securing and assigning the needed human resources to work on project activities.

questions.question: ____ is concerned with generating, gathering, and disseminating information to formalize phase or project completion.
questions.explanation: Formal acceptance involves generating, gathering, and disseminating information to formalize phase or project completion.

questions.question: ______ involves collecting and disseminating performance information to provide stakeholders with information about how resources are being used to achieve project objectives.
questions.explanation: Performance reporting involves collecting and disseminating performance information about resource utilization and objective achievement.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the Importance of Good Communications
options: The greatest threat to many projects is a failure to communicate
Research shows that SW professionals must be able to communicate effectively to succeed in their positions
