Strong verbal skill is a key factor in career advancement for SW professionals
questions.explanation: All statements highlight the importance of good communication in project management and software development careers.

questions.question: Which one of the following is False about risk management and process
options: The goal of project risk management is to minimize potential risks while maximizing potential opportunities
Risk management planning: deciding how to approach and plan the risk management activities for the project
Risk identification: determining which risks are likely to affect a project and documenting their characteristics
Many projects not include contingency plans, fallback plans, and contingency reserves.
questions.explanation: This is false because many projects do include contingency plans, fallback plans, and contingency reserves as part of risk management.

questions.question: Which one of the following is False
options: A decision tree is a diagramming method used to help you select the best course of action in situations.
Expected Monetary Value (EMV) is a type of decision tree.
Decision trees are used for quantitative risk analysis.
All of the above are true
questions.explanation: EMV is not a type of decision tree; it's a calculation method used with decision trees. Decision trees are diagramming methods for selecting the best course of action.

questions.question: Which one of the following is true
options: Project Procurement Management includes the processes required to acquire goods and services, to attain project scope, from outside the performing organization.
Procurement Planning is determining what to procure, when, and how.
Expert technical judgment will often be required to assess the inputs
questions.explanation: All statements are true about Procurement Management - acquisition of goods/services, procurement planning, and need for expert judgment.

questions.question: Which of the following is not project management goal?
options: Delivering the software to the customer at the agreed time
Maintaining a happy and well-functioning development team
questions.explanation: Avoiding customer complaints is not a project management goal. Goals focus on delivering within cost, time, and quality constraints while maintaining team morale.

questions.question: Which of the following is not considered as a risk in project management?
questions.explanation: Testing is a project activity, not a risk. Specification delays, product competition, and staff turnover are risks to be managed.

questions.question: Quality planning is the process of developing a quality plan for
questions.explanation: Quality planning develops a quality management plan for the project, defining quality standards and how they will be met.

questions.question: The project life cycle consists of
options: Understanding the scope of the project
questions.explanation: The project life cycle consists of Initiation, Planning, Execution, and Closure phases. Scope and objectives are part of planning.

questions.question: Project performance consists of
questions.explanation: Project performance is measured by time, cost, and quality - the triple constraint of project management.

questions.question: The scope of the work is defined in which phase of the project management?
questions.explanation: The scope of work is defined during the Planning phase, where detailed requirements and deliverables are established.

questions.question: During project estimation, project manager estimates following
questions.explanation: Project managers estimate duration, effort, and cost during the project estimation phase.

questions.question: A 60.0% risk is considered as
questions.explanation: A 60% probability risk is considered High risk, as it has a strong likelihood of occurring.

questions.question: When does the testing process stops?
options: When resources (time and budget) are over
questions.explanation: Testing stops when the quality criteria are met. Testing should not simply stop due to resource constraints or arbitrary coverage.

questions.question: Apple factory wants to develop mobile application. Which mobile platform is recommended for Apple company?
questions.explanation: Apple develops applications for their own iOS platform. Android is for Android devices, SDK is a development toolkit.

questions.question: Which is correct packet we install for android sdk tools?
questions.explanation: All listed components are needed for Android SDK tools - Build-tools, Support Repository, Support Library, and Google Repository.

questions.question: When user should be able to move from one network to another network and use same service
questions.explanation: User mobility allows users to move between networks while maintaining service continuity, keeping the same identity.

questions.question: What are major systems GSM network including?
questions.explanation: GSM networks include all three major systems: Switching System, Base Station System, and Operation and Support System.

questions.question: An explosive grows in mobile application stores such as apple store, google play store, windows marketing store was coupled with availability of games, utility and others apps. Which key drivers are used for mobile application?
questions.explanation: The mobile ecosystem (app stores, developers, users) drives growth in mobile applications, supported by social networking, consumer behavior, and innovation.

questions.question: Which of the following disappearing (no body will notice its presence) every place in computing environments?
questions.explanation: Ubiquitous computing is characterized by technology that disappears into the environment, making computing available everywhere without being noticed.

questions.question: Which of the following is mobile app factors?
questions.explanation: Mobile app factors include UI/UX design, security, and monitoring - all critical aspects of mobile application development.

questions.question: App Development Principles
options: Compatibility on various devices and platforms
User loyalty through targeted and personalized offers
questions.explanation: App development principles include compatibility across devices, productive user flows, user loyalty through personalization, and customer conversion.

questions.question: ____ is Google's portable UI toolkit for building beautiful, natively-compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase.
questions.explanation: Flutter is Google's UI toolkit for building natively compiled applications for mobile, web, and desktop from a single codebase.

questions.question: What is an activity in android?
options: a single screen in application with supporting java code
questions.explanation: An Activity is a single screen in an Android application with supporting Java code, representing a user interface component.

questions.question: Choice correct option related to android
questions.explanation: Android is primarily an operating system for mobile devices, not a web browser or web server.

questions.question: For which of the following Android is mainly developed?
questions.explanation: Android is mainly developed for smartphones and tablets, though it's also used in other devices like TVs and wearables.

questions.question: Which of the following virtual machine is used by the Android operating system?
questions.explanation: Android uses the Dalvik Virtual Machine (DVM) or Android Runtime (ART) to execute applications, optimized for mobile devices.

questions.question: APK stands for
questions.explanation: APK stands for Android Package Kit, the file format used for distributing and installing Android applications.

questions.question: On which of the following, developers can test the application, during developing the android applications?
questions.explanation: Developers can test Android apps on physical devices, the Android SDK emulator, or third-party emulators.

questions.question: Which of the following is contained in the src folder?
questions.explanation: The src folder contains Java source code files. XML files are in res folders, and manifest is in the app directory.

questions.question: Which of the following android component displays the part of an activity on screen?
questions.explanation: A Fragment displays a portion of an Activity's user interface, making reusable UI components and supporting multiple screen sizes.

questions.question: Identify the language on which Android is based upon.
questions.explanation: Android is primarily based on Java, with native code in C/C++. Java is the main language for Android application development.

questions.question: All layout classes are the subclasses of
questions.explanation: Layout classes extend ViewGroup, which is a subclass of View. ViewGroup can contain and arrange other views.

questions.question: What is manifest XML in android?
options: It is an information about layout in application
It has all the information about an application
It has the information about activity in an application
questions.explanation: Manifest XML contains all essential information about the application, including components, permissions, and configuration.

questions.question: Identify the topmost layer of Android architecture
questions.explanation: The Application layer is the topmost layer, containing user-facing apps. The stack is: Apps -> Framework -> Libraries/Runtime -> Linux Kernel.

questions.question: Identify among the following which is not a state in the service lifecycle.
questions.explanation: 'Pause' is not a service state. Service states are Started, Bound, and Destroyed. Activities have pause states.

questions.question: Identify the dialogue class in Android among the following
questions.explanation: All are dialog classes in Android: DatePickerDialog, AlertDialog, and ProgressDialog are all dialog types.

questions.question: Choose the built-in database of Android.
questions.explanation: SQLite is the built-in database in Android, providing a lightweight relational database for application data storage.

questions.question: Identify the layout in which Android arranges its children into rows and columns.
questions.explanation: TableLayout arranges children in rows and columns, similar to an HTML table structure.

questions.question: What are the functionalities in asyncTask in android?
questions.explanation: doInBackground() is the main method for background processing. Other methods include onPreExecute(), onProgressUpdate(), and onPostExecute().

questions.question: What is the life cycle of broadcast receivers in android?
questions.explanation: Broadcast receivers have the onReceive() method as their lifecycle. They respond to broadcasts and don't have complex lifecycle states.

questions.question: Which permissions are required to get a location in android?
questions.explanation: Both ACCESS_FINE_LOCATION (GPS) and ACCESS_COARSE_LOCATION (network) permissions are needed for location access in Android.

questions.question: Point out the wrong statement.
options: Voice Actions for Android is a voice command and speech recognition program
Google is used for local search
Google Chrome to Phone Extension sends links and information from a Chrome browser to an Android phone
questions.explanation: All statements are correct - Voice Actions, Google local search, and Chrome to Phone extension are all Android features.

questions.question: What is splash screen in android?
questions.explanation: A splash screen is the initial screen shown when an app launches, while the app loads its resources and prepares the UI.

questions.question: The process of transferring a mobile station from one base station to another is
questions.explanation: Handoff (or handover) is the process of transferring a mobile station from one base station to another during a call.

questions.question: IMEI stands for
questions.explanation: IMEI stands for International Mobile Equipment Identity, a unique number for identifying mobile devices.

questions.question: In which directory xml layout files are stored
questions.explanation: XML layout files are stored in the /res/layout directory. Values go in /res/values, source in /src, and assets in /assets.

questions.question: What is contained within layout xml file
options: orientation and layout that specify what the display look like
the code which is compiled to run the app
questions.explanation: Layout XML files contain layout specifications, orientation, and UI elements that determine how the display looks.

questions.question: The emulator device for android
options: Runs the same code base as actual device, all the way down to machine layer
is more of simulator, acts as virtual machine for android device
Runs the same code base as actual device, however at higher level
An imaginary machine built on the hope and dreams of baby elephant
questions.explanation: Android emulator runs the same code base as actual devices, using virtualization to emulate ARM architecture, down to the machine layer.

questions.question: What is XML stand for?
questions.explanation: XML stands for Extensible Markup Language, used for structuring and describing data in Android and many other applications.

questions.question: What shares the information among applications in Android?
questions.explanation: Content Providers share data between applications, providing a standard interface for accessing data from different apps.

questions.question: What handles background application processing?
questions.explanation: Services handle background processing, running long-running operations without a user interface.

questions.question: A formatted label of text is displayed by ____?
questions.explanation: TextView displays formatted text to the user. It's the basic component for displaying text in Android.

questions.question: ____ contains various items?
questions.explanation: ListView displays a scrollable list of items, allowing users to view and interact with multiple data items.

questions.question: ____ handles the interaction of users to the screen of smartphones?
questions.explanation: Activities handle user interaction with the screen, managing the UI and responding to user input.

questions.question: What are the resources in Android?
questions.explanation: Android resources include strings, drawable pictures, constants, and other static content that can be used in the app.

questions.question: What is the purpose of an AVDs manager in Android?
questions.explanation: AVD Manager creates and manages Android Virtual Devices, but deletion might be manual. Creation and management are its main functions.

questions.question: What are the services included in the Application Framework?
questions.explanation: All are services in Application Framework: Activity Manager, Notification Manager, Package Manager, and many others.

questions.question: Which layer is known as the heart of Android's architecture?
questions.explanation: The Linux Kernel is considered the heart of Android's architecture, providing core system services and hardware abstraction.

questions.question: ____ in Android is based upon manipulating directly?
questions.explanation: The interface in Android can be directly manipulated by developers to create custom user experiences.

questions.question: ____ is stores the data related to the user and is relevant to GSM (Global System for Mobile communication) mobile systems as well.
questions.explanation: SIM stores user-related data and is used in GSM systems for subscriber identification and authentication.

questions.question: Which of the following are the limitations of mobile devices?
options: The keypad is smaller as compared to the desktop
questions.explanation: All are limitations of mobile devices - rapid power consumption, smaller keypads/input, and potential for constant distraction.

questions.question: How to upgrade SQLite the database from a lower version to higher version in android SQLite?
questions.explanation: SQLiteOpenHelper class's onUpgrade() method handles database version upgrades in Android SQLite.

questions.question: Which of the following is incorrect about intents?
options: They can be used to start an Activity
They can be used to start database insertion
They can be used to start a service
They can be used to start a dialog-themed activity
questions.explanation: Intents can't directly start database insertion. They are used for starting Activities, Services, and launching dialog-themed activities.

questions.question: Which one of the following is global configuration mode?
questions.explanation: Router(config)# is the global configuration mode where system-wide settings are configured. Other modes are for specific interface/line configuration.

questions.question: Which one of the following VLAN is the default switch configuration management controls all available ports?
questions.explanation: VLAN 1 is the default VLAN on switches, where all ports belong by default. It's also the default management VLAN.

questions.question: ____ is a LED which Shows whether the system is receiving power and is functioning properly?
questions.explanation: System LED indicates power status and proper functioning. Status LED shows link status, Duplex shows duplex mode, and Speed shows link speed.

questions.question: How many end device can support a switch having 24 ports?
questions.explanation: A 24-port switch can support 24 end devices (one per port), assuming no uplink ports are used for connections.

questions.question: What is the need of configuring line console 0 interface?
options: To secure switch/router from unauthorized remote user
To secure switch/router from direct connected unauthorized user
To assign IP address for VLAN
questions.explanation: Console line configuration secures the switch/router from unauthorized users who have direct physical console access.

questions.question: What is the need of configuring line vty 0 4 interface in switch or router?
options: To secure switch/router from remote unauthorized user
To manage from directly connected device
questions.explanation: VTY (Virtual Terminal) lines are configured to secure remote access via Telnet/SSH, preventing unauthorized remote users.

questions.question: What is the need of assigning IP address for VLAN switch device?
questions.explanation: Assigning an IP address to a VLAN interface (SVI) enables remote management of the switch via Telnet/SSH/SNMP.

questions.question: Which one of the following is correct about devices MAC address?
options: MAC address is the logical address of the device
MAC address is the physical address of the host
questions.explanation: MAC address is the physical address of the device, assigned by the manufacturer. It's 48-bit long, not a logical address.

questions.question: What is the function of ping command?
options: Used to check connectivity between two end devices
It is a routing protocol used to route packet
Used to show mac address of a device
Used to show ip address of a device
questions.explanation: Ping checks connectivity between two end devices by sending ICMP echo requests and waiting for replies.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not mac address security type?
questions.explanation: Hybrid secure MAC address is not a standard type. Switch security uses Static, Dynamic, and Sticky secure MAC addresses.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not port security violation mode?
questions.explanation: Reboot is not a port security violation mode. The modes are Shutdown, Protect, and Restrict. Shutdown disables the port.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not benefit of using VLAN?
questions.explanation: Difficult to manage is a disadvantage, not a benefit of VLANs. Benefits include security, cost reduction, and performance.

questions.question: Which one of the following cable used to connect between switch and end devices?
questions.explanation: Straight-through cable connects end devices to switches. Crossover connects similar devices, and console/rollover are for configuration.

questions.question: What is the use of Copy Running-config startup-config command in Cisco router/ Switch configuration?
options: To show the default IOS configuration
questions.explanation: Copy running-config startup-config saves the current running configuration to NVRAM, making it persistent across reboots.

questions.question: Which of the following cable is used to connect between two routers?
questions.explanation: Serial cables connect two routers via their serial interfaces for WAN connections. Console cables are for configuration.

questions.question: What is the use of Banner motd Command in cisco Router configuration?
options: To set password for virtual line
To set welcome message of the day
questions.explanation: Banner motd sets the Message of the Day banner displayed before login, used for legal warnings or informational messages.

questions.question: What is the default gateway address of a host?
options: The IP address of a host
The IP address of central device
The IP address of a router
questions.explanation: Default gateway is the IP address of a router that connects the host to other networks. It's the next-hop for outbound traffic.

questions.question: Which one of the following routing protocol is Classful routing protocol?
questions.explanation: RIPv1 is a classful routing protocol that does not send subnet mask information in updates. Others are classless.

questions.question: Which one of following is not cisco router accessing ports?
questions.explanation: All are Cisco router access ports - Console, Auxiliary (AUX), and Virtual Terminal (VTY) lines for remote access.

questions.question: Which of the following command used to enter the global configuration mode?
questions.explanation: 'configure terminal' enters global configuration mode from privileged EXEC mode. 'Enable' enters privileged mode.

questions.question: Which one of the following router configuration command used to view the initial configuration of the router?
questions.explanation: 'show running-config' displays the current configuration. Startup-config shows saved config. Both can show initial config.

questions.question: If you want to display cisco 2960 switch IOS information, which one of the following command is important for your task.
questions.explanation: 'show version' displays IOS version, uptime, and hardware information for Cisco switches and routers.

questions.question: In which configuration mode you are while configuring a cisco 2600 router interfaces.
questions.explanation: Interface configuration mode is Router(config-if)#, entered after 'interface' command. Used for interface-specific settings.

questions.question: Which one of the following password protects you from accessing router interfaces vty 04.
questions.explanation: Virtual terminal password (vty password) protects Telnet/SSH access to the router. Console password is for physical access.

questions.question: Assume that mr. Alexander is a network administrator at wachemo university, he want to make disable all ports of the switches to reconfigure again. So which one of the following configuration mode and command is correct to disable all ports of the switches.
questions.explanation: Use interface range mode to select all ports and 'shutdown' command to disable them. The prompt shows config-if-range.

questions.question: Asume that in your computer laboratory class you have one switch called S1 and now you want to create 4 vlans (VLAN 10, VLAN 20, VLAN 30 and VLAN 99) from that switch, the vlan name of VLAN 99 is students. So which one of the following is correct about assigning vlan name students.
questions.explanation: In VLAN configuration mode, use 'name' command to assign the VLAN name. The prompt shows S1(config-vlan)#.

questions.question: If you want to verify VLANs are created, which of the following command is going to used.
questions.explanation: 'show vlan brief' displays a concise list of all VLANs with their ports. It's the most commonly used command for VLAN verification.

questions.question: If you want to assign switch port 6 to 15 for VLAN 99, which one of the following configuration is correct to achieve your goal on switch S3?
options:
S3(config)#interface range fa0/6-15
S3(config-if-range)#switchport access vlan 99

S3(config)#assign switch port 6-15
S3(config-if-range)#switchport access vlan 99
questions.explanation: The correct syntax uses 'interface range fa0/6-15' to select ports, then 'switchport access vlan 99' to assign them to VLAN 99.

questions.question: ____ is used for taking a packet from one device and sending it through the network to another device on a different network.
questions.explanation: Routing is the process of forwarding packets between different networks. Switching handles traffic within the same network.

questions.question: Which one of the following is the physical address of a host while in a network?
questions.explanation: MAC address is the physical address of a host, burned into the network interface card. IP address is a logical address.

questions.question: Which one of the following is important to route a router need to know?
questions.explanation: Routers need to know about remote networks, neighbor routers, and the best route to reach destinations.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not advantages of static routing.
options: No overload on the router CPU
questions.explanation: All are advantages of static routing - no CPU overload, no bandwidth usage, and better security since routes are manually configured.

questions.question: Which one of the following is example of classful routing protocols
questions.explanation: IGRP is a classful routing protocol (Cisco proprietary). EIGRP, OSPF, and IS-IS are classless protocols.

questions.question: Which one of the following is powerful feature of Enhanced Interior Gateway Routing Protocol (EIGRP).
options: Support for IP, IPX, and AppleTalk via protocol-dependent modules
Best path selection via Diffusing update algorithm (DUAL)
questions.explanation: EIGRP features include support for multiple protocols, efficient neighbor discovery, RTP for reliable communication, and DUAL for best path selection.

questions.question: If you want to discover the neighbor router EIGRP IP address, which one of the following command is useful.
questions.explanation: 'show ip eigrp neighbors' displays neighbor router IP addresses and adjacency information for EIGRP.

questions.question: Which one of the following statement not determine open shortest path first (OSPF) protocol.
options: It supports both IPv4 and IPv6
It is interior gateway routing protocol
questions.explanation: OSPF doesn't necessarily provide the fastest convergence (EIGRP is faster). It supports IPv4/IPv6, classless routing, VLSM, and is an IGP.

questions.question: Which one of the following security mechanism will you expose for external attacks
questions.explanation: Disabling the firewall exposes the network to external attacks. Firewalls are essential security mechanisms for perimeter defense.

questions.question: What is the purpose of using access-list command in router configuration?
options: Used to permit or deny packets moving through the router
Permit or deny Telnet (VTY) access to or from a router
Create dial-on demand (DDR) interesting traffic that triggers dialing to a remote location
questions.explanation: Access-lists have multiple purposes: packet filtering, VTY access control, and defining interesting traffic for DDR.

questions.question: Which one of the following is incorrect about the benefit of network address translation(NAT)
options: It can expose for security attack by hiding the internal network structure
You need to connect to the Internet and your hosts don't have globally unique IP addresses.
You change to a new ISP that requires you to renumber your network.
IT need to merge two intranets with duplicate addresses.
questions.explanation: This is incorrect - NAT actually enhances security by hiding internal network structure, not exposing it to attacks.

questions.question: If you need to clear the router configuration information, which one of the following command is correct?
questions.explanation: 'erase startup-config' clears the saved configuration from NVRAM. The configuration is stored in NVRAM, not directly erased with 'clear'.

questions.question: Which one of the following cable is used to connect computer to router using console port.
questions.explanation: Rollover cable (console cable) connects a computer's serial port to the router's console port for initial configuration.

questions.question: Which one of the following component is found inside the router
questions.explanation: Routers contain CPU, ROM, RAM, and an operating system (IOS) - all essential components found inside the router.

questions.question: ____ is used to finds the hardware address of a host from a known IP address.
questions.explanation: ARP (Address Resolution Protocol) resolves IP addresses to MAC addresses, finding the hardware address from a known IP.

questions.question: If a router can't send an IP datagram any further, it uses ICMP to send a message back to the sender, so what is the appropriate message that will be send back to the sender?
questions.explanation: ICMP 'Destination Unreachable' message is sent when a router cannot forward an IP datagram to its destination.

questions.question: ____ is the protocol that automatically assigns a host a valid IP address for the hosts.
questions.explanation: DHCP (Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol) automatically assigns IP addresses to hosts, simplifying network administration.

questions.question: MAC addresses that are automatically learned and stored only in the address table is called
questions.explanation: Dynamic secure MAC addresses are automatically learned and stored in the MAC address table. They are not permanently saved.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not switch port security violation mode
questions.explanation: Hibernate is not a port security violation mode. The valid modes are Protect, Restrict, and Shutdown.

questions.question: Which one of the following reasons are correct to create VLAN
options: Grouping users by department instead of by physical location,
Segmenting devices into smaller LANs to reduce processing overhead for all devices on LAN,
Enforcing better security by isolating sensitive data to separate VLANs,
Separating IP voice traffic from data traffic.
questions.explanation: All are valid reasons to create VLANs: logical grouping, segmentation, security, and traffic separation.

questions.question: Which one of the following is benefits of using VLAN
questions.explanation: VLANs provide security, cost reduction (fewer physical switches), and higher performance through better traffic management.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not features of route in routing table
questions.explanation: 'Route' is not a feature of a routing table entry. The table includes destination network, next hop, metric, and exit interface.

questions.question: Which of the following cannot characterize a system?
questions.explanation: All options characterize a system - components, purpose, and interfaces are all essential elements of any system.

questions.question: Which of the following UML diagram emphasizes on object interaction?
questions.explanation: Sequence diagram emphasizes object interaction by showing messages exchanged between objects over time.

questions.question: ____ is a standard set of steps/phases one passes through in system development.
questions.explanation: SDLC (System Development Life Cycle) is the standard set of phases in system development, from planning to maintenance.

questions.question: Which of the following should be considered during system's user interface design?
questions.explanation: UI design considerations include color choice, layout design, and user friendliness - all important for good user experience.

questions.question: ____ is the initial working version of the complete system.
questions.explanation: A prototype is the initial working version of a system, used for demonstration and feedback before final development.

questions.question: Which of the following can be the possible reason why system maintenance is needed?
options: To come up with alternative solution
questions.explanation: System maintenance is needed to fix failures, enhance functionality, and adapt to changes. Determining user needs is done in analysis phase.

questions.question: Which of the following feasibility analysis is associated with the financial benefits and costs during information systems development?
questions.explanation: Economic feasibility analyzes costs and financial benefits of the system. Technical feasibility examines technology, operational examines user acceptance.

questions.question: Designing how a user navigates in the developed system is represented by
questions.explanation: User interface flow diagramming represents navigation patterns, showing how users move through system interfaces.

questions.question: ____ is a form of testing in which each individual module is tested.
questions.explanation: Unit testing tests individual modules/components in isolation. Integration tests module combinations, and system tests the complete system.

questions.question: What is the fundamental purpose of system testing?
options: To evaluate whether the developed system fulfills the requirements
questions.explanation: System testing verifies that the developed system meets all specified requirements and functions as intended.

questions.question: Which of the following system acceptance testing is conducted in real environment with real and live data?
questions.explanation: Beta testing is conducted in real environment with live data. Alpha testing occurs in controlled environment at developer's site.

questions.question: Which of the following system installation approach uses the new system to run along with the old system?
questions.explanation: Parallel installation runs new system alongside the old system, comparing results before switching completely.

questions.question: Which of the following document records how to use the developed system/application?
questions.explanation: User manual documents how to use the system from an end-user perspective, including procedures and instructions.

questions.question: Which of the following activity is performed during implementation phase of system development life cycle?
questions.explanation: Coding is performed during implementation phase. Requirements and design are done earlier, scope definition is in planning.

questions.question: Which of the following types of maintenance is conducted to fix defects in the design, implementation of the system?
questions.explanation: Corrective maintenance fixes defects and errors in the system. Adaptive maintenance adjusts to environmental changes.

questions.question: In class diagram modeling, the bottom section of the diagram represents
questions.explanation: The bottom section of a class diagram contains methods (operations) of the class. Top is class name, middle is attributes.

questions.question: ____ is a measure of how two items, such as classes or methods, are interrelated.
questions.explanation: Coupling measures interrelationship between classes/methods. Cohesion measures intra-module relationship. Abstraction/encapsulation are other OOP principles.

questions.question: Which of the following is the benefit of object orientation?
questions.explanation: Object orientation provides reusability, extensibility, and reduced maintenance burden through inheritance and polymorphism.

questions.question: Which of the following software development process model states that 'the next phase of system development should begin after the completion of the preceding phase'?
questions.explanation: Waterfall model requires completion of each phase before moving to next, with sequential progression and no overlapping.

questions.question: What is the end result of implementation phase?
questions.explanation: Implementation phase results in a working system that can be tested and deployed to users.

questions.question: ____ is a process of collecting the user needs to solve a problem or issues and to achieve system objective.
questions.explanation: Requirement gathering is the process of collecting user needs and requirements for the system.

questions.question: Which of the following defines the system's quality characteristics?
questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements define system quality characteristics like performance, security, and reliability. Functional requirements define what the system does.

questions.question: Which of the following requirement gathering technique is used to gather information by which requirement gathering team sit down with concerned stakeholders and asks some questions?
questions.explanation: Interview involves direct conversation with stakeholders to gather requirements through questions and discussion.

questions.question: In relational database model, each column in a relation corresponds to
questions.explanation: Each column in a relation corresponds to an attribute (field), while each row corresponds to a record (tuple).

questions.question: Which of the following is not included under user interface design?
questions.explanation: Database design is separate from UI design. UI design covers layouts, help options, and feedback mechanisms.

questions.question: When you test the system, what are you actually testing?
questions.explanation: Testing covers all aspects - requirements verification, security testing, and performance evaluation.

questions.question: In a sequence diagram, what do the vertical dashed lines represent?
questions.explanation: Vertical dashed lines in sequence diagrams represent object lifelines, showing the duration of an object's existence.

questions.question: Consider you are transferring money to your friend's account using mobile banking system, if the system asks you 'Enter Account Number: ' while making a transfer, which type of feedback is the system providing you?
questions.explanation: 'Enter Account Number' is a prompting cue that guides the user on what input to provide next.

questions.question: Which of the following is the criterion to classify and rank the projects to be selected?
questions.explanation: Project selection criteria include potential benefits, available resources, and project duration.

questions.question: Designing and building a scaled-down but working version of the desired system is known as
questions.explanation: Prototyping builds a scaled-down working version to validate requirements and gather feedback.

questions.question: ____ is a short document prepared primarily for clearly describing what the project will deliver and outline generally at a high level all the work required for completing the project.
questions.explanation: Project scope statement describes project deliverables and outlines work required, providing a high-level view of the project.

questions.question: Which of the following can be source of information during requirement gathering?
questions.explanation: Requirement gathering sources include users, existing reports, and documented procedures and policies.

questions.question: Which of the following mechanism enables reusability in object orientated paradigm?
questions.explanation: Inheritance enables reusability by allowing derived classes to inherit and extend base class functionality.

questions.question: Which of the following characterizes non-functional requirements?
questions.explanation: Non-functional requirements include portability, reliability, performance, and other quality attributes.

questions.question: Which of the following requirement validation technique involves a meeting where you gather all of your stakeholders together and go through the requirements documentation, page-by-page, line-by-line, to ensure that the document represents everyone's complete understanding of what is to be accomplished in a particular project?
questions.explanation: Walkthrough involves reviewing requirements documentation page-by-page with stakeholders to ensure common understanding.

questions.question: Which of the following system/software testing method requires that the evaluator needs to possess knowledge of the internal working of the code?
questions.explanation: White box testing requires knowledge of internal code structure, paths, and logic. Black box testing focuses on inputs/outputs.

questions.question: Which of the following represents transitions between activities in modeling activity diagram?
questions.explanation: Arrow lines represent transitions between activities in activity diagrams. Diamond shapes are decision points, rounded rectangles are activities.

questions.question: Which of the following UML diagram is equivalent to DFD diagram from structural paradigm?
questions.explanation: Activity diagram is equivalent to Data Flow Diagram (DFD) as both show process flow and data movement.

questions.question: Which of the following is the correct sequence of system development life cycle phases?
questions.explanation: Correct SDLC sequence is: Requirement Elicitation -> Analysis -> Design -> Implementation -> Testing.

questions.question: ____ is the process of breaking down a system into its smaller components.
questions.explanation: Decomposition is the process of breaking down a system into smaller, more manageable components.

questions.question: ____ is a graphical representation of a project that shows each task as a horizontal bar whose length is proportional to its time for completion.
questions.explanation: Gantt chart shows project tasks as horizontal bars with lengths proportional to duration, used for project scheduling.

questions.question: Which of the following diagram is used in process modeling from structural paradigm point of view?
questions.explanation: Data Flow Diagram (DFD) is used for process modeling in structural paradigm, showing data flow through processes.

questions.question: Which of the following is an indication of the degree of relationship between class diagrams?
questions.explanation: Cardinality ratio indicates the degree of relationship between classes (e.g., one-to-one, one-to-many).

questions.question: Consider you have Student class diagram, which of the following can possibly exemplify the method in this diagram?
questions.explanation: viewExamResult() is a method (behavior) in Student class. Name, ID, and Age are attributes (properties).

questions.question: Which of the following type of testing is conducted to assess if the organization/user is willing to use your system?
questions.explanation: Acceptance testing assesses user willingness to accept and use the system, conducted by end users.

questions.question: Based on the above diagram, YELLOW numbers indicate
questions.explanation: In use case diagrams, actors are represented as stick figures or symbols that interact with the system.

questions.question: From the given diagram, GREEN numbers show
questions.explanation: Associations in use case diagrams connect actors to use cases, indicating interaction between them.

questions.question: From the diagram, numbers 1 and 2 indicate
questions.explanation: Numbers 1 and 2 represent associations (lines) connecting actors to use cases in the use case diagram.

questions.question: From the above diagram, the RED number is indicating
questions.explanation: The red number indicates system boundary, which separates the system from its external environment in use case diagrams.

questions.question: According to use case diagram notations, number 3 shows
questions.explanation: Number 3 shows the system name, typically placed inside the system boundary box in use case diagrams.

questions.question: Identify the term which denotes that only authorized users are capable of accessing the information
questions.explanation: Confidentiality ensures that information is accessible only to those authorized to access it, protecting against unauthorized access.

questions.question: Which of the following platforms is used for the safety and protection of information in the cloud?
questions.explanation: Cloud workload protection is specifically designed for security and protection of information in cloud environments.

questions.question: Choose among the following techniques, which are used to hide information inside a picture.
questions.explanation: Steganography is the technique of hiding information within other media like images, making the hidden data undetectable.

questions.question: Which protocol is mostly used in Wi-fi security?
questions.explanation: All these protocols are used in Wi-Fi security: WPS (Wi-Fi Protected Setup), WPA, and WPA2 (the most secure).

questions.question: Which type of malware does not replicate or clone through an infection?
questions.explanation: Trojans do not replicate or clone themselves. They disguise as legitimate software, while viruses and worms replicate.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as with the least strong security encryption.
questions.explanation: WEP (Wired Equivalent Privacy) is the least secure encryption standard, easily crackable and outdated.

questions.question: Which of the following is used for encrypting data at the network level?
questions.explanation: IPSec (Internet Protocol Security) encrypts data at the network level, securing IP communications.

questions.question: Identify the type of symmetric key algorithm which uses a streaming cipher to encrypt information.
questions.explanation: RC4 is a symmetric stream cipher, encrypting data one byte at a time. SHA and MD5 are hash functions, Blowfish is a block cipher.

questions.question: Which of the following is considered as the unsolicited commercial email?
questions.explanation: Spam is unsolicited commercial email sent in bulk, often considered junk email.

questions.question: Which one of the following can be considered as the class of computer threats?
questions.explanation: Phishing is a class of computer threat where attackers trick users into revealing sensitive information.

questions.question: Identify the term which denotes the protection of data from modification by unknown users.
questions.explanation: Integrity ensures data is protected from unauthorized modification, maintaining its accuracy and trustworthiness.

questions.question: Who is the father of computer security?
questions.explanation: August Kerckhoffs is considered the father of computer security for his contributions to cryptography and security principles.

questions.question: Which of the following is not a cybercrime?
questions.explanation: AES (Advanced Encryption Standard) is an encryption algorithm, not a cybercrime. The others are common cyber attacks.

questions.question: Governments hired some highly skilled hackers for providing cyber security for the country or state. These types of hackers are termed as
questions.explanation: Nation/State sponsored hackers are hired by governments to provide cybersecurity and conduct defensive/offensive operations.

questions.question: Which of the following is the hacking approach where cyber-criminals design fake websites or pages for tricking or gaining additional traffic?
questions.explanation: Pharming redirects users to fake websites by manipulating DNS or hosts files to steal credentials.

questions.question: A cyber-criminal or penetration tester uses the additional data that stores certain special instructions in the memory for activities to break the system in which of the following attack?
questions.explanation: Buffer-overflow attacks exploit memory by storing extra data that overflows the buffer, containing instructions to compromise the system.

questions.question: Which of the following is defined as an attempt to harm, damage or cause threat to a system or network?
questions.explanation: Cyber Attack is defined as an attempt to harm, damage, or threaten a system or network infrastructure.

questions.question: They are nefarious hackers, and their main motive is to gain financial profit by doing cybercrimes. Who are 'they' referred to here?
questions.explanation: Black Hat Hackers are malicious hackers who break into systems for personal gain, often financial profit.

questions.question: Which of the following is an internet scam done by cyber-criminals where the user is convinced digitally to provide confidential information.
questions.explanation: Phishing attacks trick users into providing confidential information through deceptive emails or websites.

questions.question: Which of the following ethical hacking technique is used for determining which operating system (OS) is running on a remote computer?
questions.explanation: OS fingerprinting determines the operating system running on a remote computer by analyzing responses to various packets.

questions.question: Which of the following can diminish the chance of data leakage?
questions.explanation: Cryptography diminishes data leakage by encrypting data, making it unreadable without the decryption key.

questions.question: A security manager is setting up resource permissions in an application. The security manager has discovered that he can establish objects that contain access permissions, and then assign individual users to those objects. The access control model that most closely resembles this is:
questions.explanation: RBAC (Role Based Access Control) involves creating roles with permissions and assigning users to those roles.

questions.question: A security manager needs to be able to regularly determine when operating system files change. What kind of tool is needed for this task?
questions.explanation: File system integrity monitoring tools check file changes, hashes, and detect unauthorized modifications to system files.

questions.question: A security manager needs to perform a risk assessment on a critical business application in order to determine what additional controls may be needed to protect the application and its databases. The best approach to performing this risk assessment is:
options: Perform a qualitative risk assessment only
Perform a quantitative risk assessment only
Perform a qualitative risk assessment first, then perform a quantitative risk assessment
Perform a quantitative risk assessment, then perform a qualitative risk assessment
questions.explanation: Best approach: qualitative first to identify risks, then quantitative to measure and prioritize them.

questions.question: A security manager wishes all new laptops purchased by his organization to include a security crypto processor. What hardware should be required?
questions.explanation: TPM provides hardware-based security functions including cryptographic operations and secure key storage.

questions.question: A stateful packet filtering firewall protects a web server. Which of the following is true:
options: The firewall will authenticate all users to the web server
The firewall will detect but not block application-level attacks
The firewall will block application-level attacks
The firewall will not block application-level attacks
questions.explanation: Stateful firewalls inspect network layer and transport layer, not application layer, so they can't block application-level attacks.

questions.question: A suspect has been forging credit cards with the purpose of stealing money from their owners through ATM withdrawals. Under which U.S. law is this suspect most likely to be prosecuted?
questions.explanation: Access Device Fraud covers credit card fraud and unauthorized use of access devices (credit cards).

questions.question: A system administrator needs to harden a server. The most effective approach is:
options: Install security patches and install a firewall
Remove unneeded services, remove unneeded accounts, and configure a firewall
Remove unneeded services, disable unused ports, and remove unneeded accounts
Install security patches and remove unneeded services
questions.explanation: Most effective approach: remove unneeded services, disable unused ports, and remove unneeded accounts.

questions.question: A systems engineer has discovered that a web server supports only 56-bit SSL connections. What can the systems engineer deduce from this?
options: Web communications with this server are highly secure
The server does not support remote administration
Web communications with this server are not secure
The server is running the Windows operating system
questions.explanation: 56-bit SSL is weak encryption, easily breakable, making web communications not secure.

questions.question: All of the following statements about the OSI network model are true EXCEPT:
options: No commercial network product that contains all of the components of the OSI model have ever been built
The OSI network model uses encapsulation to build communication packets
TCP/IP is an implementation of the OSI network model
The OSI network model is a model of a network protocol stack
questions.explanation: TCP/IP is not an implementation of OSI model; it predates OSI and is a different architecture.

questions.question: All of the following statements about the polyalphabetic cipher are true EXCEPT:
options: It is a form of one-time pad
It is resistant to frequency analysis attacks
It is a type of substitution cipher
questions.explanation: Polyalphabetic cipher is not a one-time pad. One-time pad uses truly random keys and is theoretically unbreakable.

questions.question: An attacker is attempting to learn the encryption key that is used to protect messages being sent between two parties. The attacker is able to create his own messages, get them encrypted by one of the parties, and can then examine the ciphertext for his message. This type of attack is known as:
questions.explanation: Chosen plaintext attack allows attacker to choose plaintext and observe resulting ciphertext to analyze encryption.

questions.question: An employee with a previous criminal history was terminated. The former employee leaked several sensitive documents to the news media. To prevent this, the organization should have:
options: Restricted the employee's access to sensitive information
Performed a background verification prior to hiring the employee
questions.explanation: Restricting access to sensitive information would have prevented this employee from accessing and leaking documents.

questions.question: An information system that processes sensitive information is configured to require a valid userid and strong password from any user. This process of accepting and validating this information is known as:
questions.explanation: Authentication is the process of verifying user identity through credentials like userid and password.

questions.question: An IT manager wishes to connect several branch offices to the headquarters office for voice and data communications. What packet switched service should the IT manager consider?
questions.explanation: MPLS (Multiprotocol Label Switching) is commonly used for connecting branch offices with voice and data over packet-switched networks.

questions.question: The PHP function ____ is used to format a time and/or date.
questions.explanation: The date() function formats a local time/date, allowing customization of how date and time are displayed.

questions.question: Which element sorts an array in sort associative array in descending order, according to the value?
questions.explanation: rsort() sorts an array in descending order by value. arsort() sorts associative arrays by value in descending order.

questions.question: When you use the $_POST variable to collect data, the data is visible to:
questions.explanation: POST data is not visible in URL (unlike GET), making it more secure and visible only to server-side scripts.

questions.question: The key difference between cookies and sessions is that cookies store data in the user's Web browsers and sessions store data on the server itself.
questions.explanation: True. Cookies store data on client-side (browser), while sessions store data on server-side for security and larger data storage.

questions.question: The fgetc() function is similar to fgets() except that it returns only a single character from a file every time it is called.
questions.explanation: True. fgetc() returns a single character, while fgets() returns a line (or specified number of characters).

questions.question: Which one of the following statements should we use to set the session username to 'Abebe'?
questions.explanation: $_SESSION['username']='Abebe'; is the correct syntax to set a session variable in PHP.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements is used to create a table in PHP?
questions.explanation: Correct SQL syntax: CREATE TABLE table_name (column_name column_type); The table name comes after CREATE TABLE.

questions.question: Conditional statements are statements that can only be executed based on the fulfillment of particular condition(s).
questions.explanation: True. Conditional statements (if, else, switch) execute code only when specified conditions are met.

questions.question: Which one of the following should not be used while sending passwords or other sensitive information?
questions.explanation: 'next' is not a valid HTTP method. GET (not recommended) and POST are methods for sending data. POST is recommended for sensitive data.

questions.question: Arrays are structured as a series of key-value pairs, where one pair is an item or element of that array.
questions.explanation: True. PHP arrays are key-value pairs, with keys being numeric (indexed) or string (associative).

questions.question: Which flag is to be passed to the function filter_var() to validate an e-mail address?
questions.explanation: FILTER_VALIDATE_EMAIL is the correct flag for email validation in PHP's filter_var() function.

questions.question: The benefit of using the GET method is that the resulting page can be bookmarked in the user's Web browser (since it's a complete URL).
questions.explanation: True. GET parameters are in the URL, making pages bookmarkable. POST data is not included in URL.

questions.question: Which statement enables you to incorporate other files into your PHP documents?
questions.explanation: include (and require) statements allow incorporating external PHP files into the current document.

questions.question: The ____ statement requires the path to an include file and otherwise behaves the same way as the include statement the first time it is called.
questions.explanation: include_once includes the file only once, preventing duplicate inclusion errors.

questions.question: Which one of the following functions requires a string that represents the path to the directory you want to create and an octal number integer (leading by 0) that represents the mode you want to set for the directory?
questions.explanation: mkdir() creates directories with specified path and mode (permissions). rmdir() removes directories.

questions.question: The ____ function accepts a file resource as an argument, as well as the number of bytes you want to read.
questions.explanation: fread() reads data from a file resource with specified number of bytes to read.

questions.question: ____ in a database is a way of requesting that the database keep an eye on the values of a specific column or combination of columns (loosely stated).
questions.explanation: An index is a database structure that improves the speed of data retrieval operations on a table.

questions.question: Which alternative is not true about identifiers?
options: Should only contain letters, numbers, and the underscore (no spaces).
Should not be the same as an existing keyword (like an SQL term or a function name).
Must be unique within its realm
questions.explanation: All statements about identifiers are true. They should follow naming conventions and be unique identifiers.

questions.question: A table's primary key is an artificial way to refer to a record and has to abide by three rules. Which one is true about those rules?
options: That value must be unique for each record in the table.
questions.explanation: Primary key must always have value (not null), must never change, and must be unique across all records.

questions.question: Conditional statements are statements that can only be executed based on the fulfillment of a particular condition(s).
questions.explanation: True. Conditional statements execute only when specified conditions are satisfied.

questions.question: Which one of the following PHP modes provides fopen() function for doing so and requires a string that contains the file path?
questions.explanation: fopen() can open files in read, write, append, and many other modes. All listed modes are valid.

questions.question: Which one of the following functions is capable of reading a file into a string variable in PHP?
questions.explanation: file_get_contents() reads a file into a string. It's the most efficient way to read file contents.

questions.question: Why we don't need to know the size of a file in PHP?
options: When someone wants to attach a file to an email or stream a file to the user.
To properly create the headers (in the case of the email).
To download some monstrous application or high-resolution photograph from your site.
questions.explanation: All scenarios require knowing file size for proper headers, attachment handling, and download progress.

questions.question: How do you get information from a PHP form that has been submitted using the GET method?
questions.explanation: $_GET[] superglobal array contains data submitted via GET method. $_POST[] is for POST, $_REQUEST includes both.

questions.question: From the following alternatives, which variable scope is not supported by PHP?
questions.explanation: Protected variables are not a PHP scope type. Global, local, and function parameters are supported.

questions.question: To upload an HTML file to a web server, we will not use the following alternatives except:
questions.explanation: FTP (File Transfer Protocol) is specifically designed for file uploads. HTTP is for web content, SMTP for email, SIP for VoIP.

questions.question: In PHP variables name should have to start with:
questions.explanation: PHP variable names must start with the dollar sign ($), followed by the variable name.

questions.question: The PHP scripts are executed on one of the following alternatives.
options: A and B are the answers
questions.explanation: PHP scripts are executed on the server side, not on the client computer.

questions.question: What is the correct way to add 1 to the $counter variable?
options: A and D are the answers
questions.explanation: Both '$counter++' and '$counter = $counter + 1' correctly increment the counter variable.

questions.question: Which data type is treated as an array in PHP?
options: A and D are the answers
questions.explanation: echo is not a data type; it's a language construct. Strings can be treated as arrays of characters.

questions.question: Which alternative is used to print statements in PHP?
options: A and D are the answers
questions.explanation: echo is the primary method for printing output in PHP. print is another option, but echo is more commonly used.

questions.question: Which one of the following alternatives contains a variable with an illegal name?
questions.explanation: $123my_Name is illegal because variable names cannot start with a number. They must start with a letter or underscore.

questions.question: In our PHP programs, if the directive session.cookie_lifetime is set to 7200, the cookie will live until:
questions.explanation: session.cookie_lifetime is measured in seconds, so 7200 seconds = 2 hours.

questions.question: What is the return type of session_set_save_handler() function?
questions.explanation: session_set_save_handler() returns a boolean value indicating success or failure.

questions.question: Which PHP function is used to erase all session variables stored in the current session?
questions.explanation: session_unset() clears all session variables. session_destroy() destroys the entire session.

questions.question: Which one of the following functions is used to start a session in PHP?
questions.explanation: session_start() is the correct function to start or resume a session in PHP.

questions.question: Which element sorts an array in ascending order?
questions.explanation: sort() sorts an array in ascending order. rsort() sorts descending. asort() sorts associative arrays by value.

questions.question: Which one of the following is not the role of the action attribute when creating forms in PHP?
options: It tells the web browser where to send the form data when the user fills out and submits the form
It allows the programmer to connect to an external HTML script
It connects the HTML script to the PHP engine
questions.explanation: Action attribute's main role is to specify where form data is sent. It doesn't directly connect to PHP engine.

questions.question: Which element sorts an array in descending order?
questions.explanation: rsort() sorts arrays in descending order. sort() sorts ascending, asort() sorts associative by value, ksort() by key.

questions.question: In PHP the ____ function checks if the 'end-of-file' (EOF) has been reached.
questions.explanation: feof() checks for end-of-file condition. It returns true when file pointer reaches EOF.

questions.question: Which PHP function is used to read a single character from a file?
questions.explanation: fgetc() reads a single character from a file. fgets() reads a line, fread() reads specified bytes.

questions.question: If the user has cookies set, we can use the ____ array to store data from one request to the next with a particular browser.
options: A and B are the answers
questions.explanation: $_SESSION array stores session data across requests, using cookies to track the session.

questions.question: What will be the output of the directive session.cookie lifetime is set to 5600?
options: The cookie will live until 5600 seconds
The cookie will live until 5600 microseconds
The cookie will live until 5600 minutes
The cookie will live until 5600 hours
questions.explanation: session.cookie_lifetime is in seconds, so 5600 seconds is the cookie lifetime.

questions.question: The ____ function is used to send a cookie to the browser.
questions.explanation: setcookie() is the correct function to send a cookie to the browser in PHP.

questions.question: What will happen to a cookie when no expiration time is explicitly set?
options: It expires when browser is closed
questions.explanation: Without explicit expiration time, cookies become session cookies and expire when browser is closed.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to maintain the value of a variable over different PHP pages?
questions.explanation: Sessions are used to persist data across multiple pages. session_register was used in older PHP (now deprecated).

questions.question: Which one of the following databases is PHP supported in the beginning?
questions.explanation: PHP initially supported MySQL for database connectivity. MySQLi and others came later.

questions.question: Which one of the following functions reads a directory into an Array in PHP?
questions.explanation: scandir() returns an array of files and directories from the specified path.

questions.question: Which one of the following methods is not responsible for sending the query to the database?
questions.explanation: query() is the standard method for sending queries. send_query() and query_send() are not standard methods.

questions.question: Which of the following lines of code allow one to remove certain session data in PHP?
questions.explanation: unset($_SESSION['lastname']) removes a specific session variable. All other variations have syntax errors.

questions.question: Which of the following is generally used for performing tasks like creating the structure of the relations, deleting relation?
questions.explanation: DDL (Data Definition Language) is used for defining database structures including creating, altering, and deleting relations.

questions.question: Which one of the following given statements possibly contains the error?
options: select empid from emp where empid = 10006;
select empid where empid = 1009 and Lastname = 'ADDIS';
questions.explanation: The last statement is missing the FROM clause. Correct syntax: SELECT empid FROM emp WHERE empid = 1009 AND Lastname = 'ADDIS';

questions.question: Which one of the following refers to the 'data about data'?
questions.explanation: Metadata is data about data, providing information about the structure, content, and context of data in the database.

questions.question: Which of the following refers to the level of data abstraction that describes exactly how the data actually stored?
questions.explanation: The Physical Level describes how data is actually stored on storage devices, including file organization and indexing.

questions.question: Which one of the following is a type of Data Manipulation Command?
questions.explanation: DELETE is a DML command used to remove data from tables. CREATE and ALTER are DDL commands.

questions.question: Which of the following is used in the application programs to request data from the database management system?
questions.explanation: DML (Data Manipulation Language) is used to request and manipulate data in the database from application programs.

questions.question: Which of the following commands is used to save any transaction permanently into the database?
questions.explanation: COMMIT saves all changes made in the current transaction permanently to the database.

questions.question: Which one of the following refers to the total view of the database content?
questions.explanation: Conceptual view provides a complete picture of the entire database, representing all entities, relationships, and constraints.

questions.question: Which of the following keys is generally used to represents the relationships between the tables?
questions.explanation: Foreign keys establish and enforce relationships between tables by referencing the primary key of another table.

questions.question: The minimal set of super key is called
questions.explanation: A primary key is the minimal super key that uniquely identifies each row in a table. Candidate keys are all possible minimal super keys.

questions.question: Which of the following in true regarding Referential Integrity?
options: Every primary-key value must match a primary-key value in an associated table
Every primary-key value must match a foreign-key value in an associated table
Every foreign-key value must match a primary-key value in an associated table
Every foreign-key value must match a foreign-key value in an associated table
questions.explanation: Referential Integrity ensures that every foreign key value in a table matches a primary key value in the referenced table.

questions.question: What are ACID properties of Transactions?
questions.explanation: ACID properties are Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, and Durability - ensuring reliable transaction processing in databases.

questions.question: A relation that has no partial dependencies is in which normal form
questions.explanation: A relation in 2NF has no partial dependencies (no non-prime attribute is dependent on part of a candidate key).

questions.question: The object definition language (ODL) is which of the following?
options: A data definition language for OODB
A method to implement a logical schema
questions.explanation: ODL is a data definition language for Object-Oriented Databases used to develop logical schemas and implement them.

questions.question: In object-oriented database, the keyword 'inverse' is used in which of the following?
questions.explanation: The 'inverse' keyword is used in relationship specifications in ODL to specify the inverse relationship between two classes.

questions.question: ____ a very important phase in designing a successful database application.
questions.explanation: Conceptual modeling is crucial for creating a high-level representation of database requirements independent of implementation details.

questions.question: ____ refers to a particular database and associated programs that implement the database queries and updates.
questions.explanation: Database application includes the database and programs designed to interact with it, handling queries and updates.

questions.question: ____ a popular high-level conceptual data model frequently used for the conceptual design of database applications.
questions.explanation: ER (Entity-Relationship) model is widely used for conceptual database design, representing entities, attributes, and relationships.

questions.question: The most widely implemented language for relational databases.
questions.explanation: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard and most widely implemented language for relational database management.

questions.question: ____ set of data whose values make up an instance of each attribute defined for that relation.
questions.explanation: A tuple (row) is a set of data values that forms an instance of attributes defined in a relation (table).

questions.question: ____ uses the terms table, column, and row to describe these items.
questions.explanation: Relational databases use the terms table, column, and row to describe the structure of data storage.

questions.question: The standard language for Relation Database System.
questions.explanation: SQL (Structured Query Language) is the standard language for relational database systems.

questions.question: The data in RDBMS is stored in database objects called ____.
questions.explanation: In RDBMS, data is stored in tables (also called relations) which organize data into rows and columns.

questions.question: Which one of the following horizontal entity in table and vertical entity in table?
questions.explanation: In tables, horizontal entities are rows (records) and vertical entities are columns (attributes).

questions.question: ____ are the rules enforced on data columns on table.
questions.explanation: SQL constraints are rules enforced on data columns in tables to ensure data integrity and validity.

questions.question: Which one uniquely identify each rows/records in a database table?
questions.explanation: Primary key uniquely identifies each row/record in a database table, ensuring no duplicate rows.

questions.question: The ____ enforces no duplication rows in a table.
questions.explanation: Entity integrity ensures each table has a unique primary key and no duplicate rows exist in the table.

questions.question: ____ enforces valid entries for a given column by restricting the type, the format, or the range of values.
questions.explanation: Domain integrity ensures that data entered in a column meets specified constraints regarding type, format, and range.

questions.question: SQL is followed by unique set of rules and guidelines called ____.
questions.explanation: SQL syntax provides the specific rules and guidelines that must be followed when writing SQL statements.

questions.question: ____ provides commands for defining databases and relation schemas, deleting relations and modifying relation schemas.
questions.explanation: DDL (Data Definition Language) provides commands like CREATE, ALTER, and DROP for defining and modifying database schemas.

questions.question: ____ used to delete existing database, table or constraints.
questions.explanation: DROP command is used to delete existing database objects like tables, databases, or constraints permanently.

questions.question: ____ used to modify the definition of the existing relation schema.
questions.explanation: ALTER command modifies the structure of existing tables by adding, deleting, or modifying columns and constraints.

questions.question: ____ includes a query language based on both the relational algebra and the tuple relational calculus.
questions.explanation: DML (Data Manipulation Language) includes query language based on relational algebra and relational calculus for data operations.

questions.question: SQL DML includes three clauses that can be used for updating the content of relations.
questions.explanation: SQL DML includes INSERT, UPDATE, and DELETE clauses for modifying the content of database relations.

questions.question: ____ it is a SQL clause used to add a number of tuples into a specified relation.
questions.explanation: INSERT statement adds new tuples (rows) into a specified relation/table in the database.

questions.question: ____ it is a clause used to delete specified tuples from a relation that meets specified criteria.
questions.explanation: DELETE statement removes specified tuples from a relation that meet the criteria specified in the WHERE clause.

questions.question: ____ an important feature in SQL Server.
questions.explanation: Data types are fundamental in SQL Server, defining the kind of data that can be stored in columns, including constraints and rules.

questions.question: Which of the following one table points to a primary key in another table?
questions.explanation: Foreign key in one table references (points to) the primary key of another table, establishing relationships between tables.

questions.question: ____ describes data as entities, relationships, and attributes.
questions.explanation: All these concepts describe data using entities (objects), relationships (associations), and attributes (properties).

questions.question: ____ is an object with a physical existence and conceptual existence.
questions.explanation: An entity is a real-world object with physical existence (like a person) or conceptual existence (like a department).

questions.question: ____ will have a value for each of its attributes.
questions.explanation: Each entity instance must have a value for each of its attributes as defined by the entity type.

questions.question: An attribute that resulted when composite and multivalued attributes are arbitrarily nested.
questions.explanation: Complex attributes result from nesting composite and multivalued attributes to represent complex data structures.

questions.question: ____ are attributes/constraints on the entities of an entity type.
questions.explanation: Keys are attributes used to uniquely identify entities, serving as constraints on entity instances.

questions.question: ____ describes participation of an entity type in a relationship type.
questions.explanation: Role describes how an entity type participates in a relationship, specifying the part played by the entity.

questions.question: ____ is an association among the instances of one or more entity types.
questions.explanation: A relationship is an association between instances of entity types, representing how entities are connected.

questions.question: Which one of the following is best match
questions.explanation: All terms are correct matches: Row=Record=Tuple (horizontal), Column=Field (vertical) in database tables.

questions.question: ____ allows us to check the value stored in the column or table in the form of range.
questions.explanation: CHECK constraint ensures that values in a column meet specified conditions or fall within a given range.

questions.question: Which Cisco IOS mode displays a prompt of Router#?
